mishnayos.summary: On the night before Pesach we search the house for chametz with a candle. This mishnah teaches which places need to be searched.

chunks.en: On the night of the fourteenth of Nisan,
chunks.st: On the evening [or] of the fourteenth of the month of Nisan,

words.note: Or means light; here it means the evening.

chunks.en: we search for chametz by the light of a candle.
chunks.st: one searches for leavened bread in his home by candlelight.

words.note: Food made from grain that rose, like bread. It is forbidden on Pesach.

chunks.en: Any place where we don't bring
chunks.st: Any place into which one does not typically take

chunks.en: chametz does not need to be searched.
chunks.st: leavened bread does not require a search,
chunks.stMore: as it is unlikely that there is any leavened bread there.

chunks.en: So why did they say to search two rows in a wine cellar?
chunks.st: And with regard to what the Sages of previous generations meant when they said that one must search two rows of wine barrels in a cellar, i.e.,

words.note: Rows of wine barrels.

chunks.en: Because it is a place where people bring chametz.
chunks.explain: Someone may go down to get more wine while holding bread.
chunks.st: a place into which one typically takes some leavened bread,
chunks.stMore: the early tanna’im are in dispute.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains why chametz is brought into the wine cellar.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of Shammai.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת עַל פְּנֵי כָל הַמַּרְתֵּף.
chunks.en: two rows across the whole front of the cellar.
chunks.st: that this is referring to searching the first two rows across the entire cellar,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

words.note: Beis Hillel are the students of Hillel.

chunks.en: the two outside rows, which are the top ones.
chunks.st: There is no need to search that extensively, as it is sufficient to search the two external rows, which are the upper ones.
chunks.stMore: This dispute will be explained and illustrated in the Gemara.

mishnayos.summary: After we search, we don't worry that a weasel dragged chametz into a place we already checked.

chunks.en: We don't worry that maybe a weasel dragged chametz
chunks.st: After conducting the search, one need not be concerned that perhaps a marten dragged leaven

words.note: A small animal, like a ferret. Steinsaltz calls it a marten.

chunks.en: from house to house or from place to place.
chunks.st: from house to house, or from place to place,
chunks.stMore: placing leaven in a house that was already searched.

chunks.en: Because if so,
chunks.st: As if so, one need also be concerned that perhaps leaven might have been dragged

chunks.en: we would worry about from yard to yard and from city to city,
chunks.st: from courtyard to courtyard and from city to city.

chunks.en: and there would be no end to it.
chunks.st: In that case, there is no end to the matter,
chunks.stMore: and it would be impossible to rely on any search for leaven.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehuda says we search for chametz three times. The Sages say that if we forgot to search at night, we still search later.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: we search on the night of the fourteenth, and on the
chunks.st: One searches for leaven on the evening of the fourteenth of Nisan, and on the fourteenth in

chunks.en: fourteenth in the morning, and at the time of burning.
chunks.st: the morning, and at the time of the removal of leaven.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: if he did not search on the night of the fourteenth,
chunks.st: that is not the case; however, if one did not search on the evening of the fourteenth he should

chunks.en: he should search on the fourteenth during the day.
chunks.st: search on the fourteenth during the day.

chunks.en: If he did not search on the fourteenth,
chunks.st: If he did not search on the fourteenth,

chunks.en: he should search during Pesach.
chunks.st: he should search during the festival of Passover.

chunks.en: If he did not search during Pesach,
chunks.st: If he did not search during the Festival,

chunks.en: he should search after Pesach.
chunks.explain: Chametz that was owned during Pesach may not be used, so it must be gotten rid of.
chunks.st: he should search after the Festival,
chunks.stMore: as any leaven that remained in his possession during the Festival is classified as leaven owned by a Jew during Passover, which one is obligated to remove.

chunks.en: And the chametz that he leaves over,
chunks.st: And the principle is: With regard to the leaven that one leaves after the search, he should

chunks.en: he should put it in a hidden place,
chunks.st: place it in a concealed location where it will most likely be left untouched,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה אַחֲרָיו:
chunks.en: so that he won't need to search for it again.
chunks.st: so that it will not require searching after it if it goes missing.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda argue until what time on Erev Pesach we may still eat chametz, and when we must burn it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says: One

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: we may eat chametz all of the fifth hour,
chunks.st: may eat leaven the entire fifth hour of the fourteenth of Nisan,

chunks.en: and we burn it at the start of the sixth hour.
chunks.st: and one must burn it immediately afterward at the beginning of the sixth hour.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: One

chunks.en: we may eat all of the fourth hour,
chunks.st: may eat the entire fourth hour

chunks.en: and during all of the fifth hour we wait,
chunks.explain: We don't eat the chametz and don't burn it yet.
chunks.st: and one places it in abeyance for the entire fifth hour,

words.note: We don't eat it and don't burn it yet.

chunks.en: and we burn it at the start of the sixth hour.
chunks.st: and one burns it at the beginning of the sixth hour.

mishnayos.stIntro: The tanna’im disagree regarding until what time leaven may be eaten and at what time it must be removed on Passover eve.

mishnayos.summary: Two loaves of bread were put on a bench in the Beis HaMikdash as a sign to everyone: while they were there, people could eat chametz; when they were taken away, it was time to burn it.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehuda also said,
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: two loaves of a korban todah that became pasul
chunks.st: Two disqualified loaves of a thanks-offering

words.note: A thanksgiving korban that comes with loaves of bread.
Not good to be used for a korban.

chunks.en: were placed on the roof of the bench.
chunks.st: are placed on the bench in the colonnade in the Temple as an indicator.
chunks.stMore: There was a specially designated place for these loaves in the Temple.

chunks.en: As long as they were lying there,
chunks.st: As long as the loaves are placed there,

chunks.en: all the people were eating chametz.
chunks.st: the entire nation continues to eat leaven.

chunks.en: When one was taken away,
chunks.st: When one of the loaves was taken away,

chunks.en: we wait: we don't eat and we don't burn.
chunks.st: the people know that the time had come to place the leaven in abeyance, meaning that they neither eat nor burn their leaven.

chunks.en: When both were taken away,
chunks.st: When they were both taken away,

chunks.en: all the people started burning their chametz.
chunks.st: the entire nation began burning their leaven.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says
chunks.stMore: that the times are divided differently:

words.note: The head of the Sages.

chunks.en: regular food may be eaten all of the fourth hour,
chunks.st: Non-sacred foods are eaten the entire fourth hour,

words.note: Food that is not holy.

chunks.en: and terumah all of the fifth hour,
chunks.explain: It is a mitzvah for Kohanim to eat terumah, so they got more time.
chunks.st: and teruma may be eaten during the entire fifth hour.
chunks.stMore: Since it is a mitzva to eat teruma and burning it is prohibited, additional time was allocated for its consumption.

words.note: The portion of food given to the Kohanim. It is holy.

chunks.en: and we burn it at the start of the sixth hour.
chunks.st: And one burns all leaven including teruma at the beginning of the sixth hour.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohanim would burn meat that was a little tamei together with meat that was very tamei, even though this made it more tamei, since it was being burned anyway.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina the deputy High Priest says:

words.note: The deputy of the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.he: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ מִלִּשְׂרֹף
chunks.en: In all the days of the Kohanim, they never held back from burning
chunks.st: In all the days of the priests, they did not refrain from burning

chunks.he: אֶת הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה עִם
chunks.en: meat that became tamei from something a little tamei, together with
chunks.st: meat that became ritually impure by coming into contact with a secondary source of ritual impurity, i.e., an object that had come into contact with a primary source of impurity, together

words.note: Something that became tamei from touching something else that is tamei.

chunks.en: meat that became tamei from something very tamei,
chunks.st: with meat that became ritually impure by contact with a primary source of impurity.

words.note: A main source of tumah, like a dead creature.

chunks.en: even though they add
chunks.st: They would do so even though they would thereby add a degree of

chunks.en: more tumah onto its tumah.
chunks.st: impurity to the impurity of the first piece of meat, which was previously impure to a lesser degree.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva added and said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva added to the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina the deputy High Priest and said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: In all the days of the Kohanim, they never held back
chunks.st: In all the days of the priests, they did not refrain

chunks.en: from lighting oil that became pasul by someone who went to the mikvah
chunks.st: from lighting teruma oil that was ritually disqualified by coming into contact with one who immersed himself

words.en: by one who went to the mikvah

chunks.en: that day, in a lamp that became tamei from a dead person,
chunks.st: during that day and who does not become completely purified until nightfall in a lamp that became ritually impure with first-degree impurity through contact with one who became ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse.

words.note: He went to the mikvah today, and is not fully tahor until night.

chunks.en: even though they add
chunks.st: They did so even though they would thereby add

chunks.en: more tumah onto its tumah.
chunks.st: impurity to the impurity of the oil.
chunks.stMore: A person who immersed himself during that day assumes the status of second-degree ritual impurity. His contact renders the oil ritually impure with third-degree ritual impurity. The lamp with first-degree ritual impurity renders the oil ritually impure with second-degree impurity.

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos the removal of leaven on Passover eve, including the consecrated loaves of thanks-offerings and teruma, the mishna cites a related halakha.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei argue whether, on Erev Pesach, we may burn terumah that is tahor together with terumah that is tamei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: From their words we learned
chunks.st: From their statements we learned

chunks.he: שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין תְּרוּמָה טְהוֹרָה עִם הַטְּמֵאָה בְּפֶסַח.
chunks.en: that we may burn tahor terumah with tamei terumah on Pesach.
chunks.st: that one may burn ritually pure teruma with impure teruma when removing leaven on Passover eve.
chunks.stMore: The rationale that applies to the two previous cases applies here as well. Since both items are being burned, one may disregard the fact that one item will assume a higher degree of ritual impurity in the process.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: That is not the right way to learn it.
chunks.explain: In those cases, both things were already tamei.
chunks.st: That is not the inference from which the halakha in the case of ritually pure and ritually impure teruma can be learned.
chunks.stMore: In those first two cases, the two items are both ritually impure, albeit at different degrees of ritual impurity. Rabbi Meir is referring to the combination of impure teruma with pure teruma, which would render pure teruma ritually impure.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree
chunks.st: And in fact Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who disagree with regard to the burning of leavened teruma, nevertheless

chunks.en: that we burn this one by itself and that one by itself.
chunks.st: concede that one burns this ritually pure teruma by itself and that impure teruma by itself.

chunks.en: About what did they argue?
chunks.st: With regard to what did they disagree?

chunks.en: About terumah that we are not sure is tahor, and about tamei terumah.
chunks.st: They disagreed with regard to whether one may burn teruma in abeyance, i.e., teruma whose purity is uncertain, and definitely impure teruma together,

chunks.en: For Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: as Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: this one should be burned by itself and that one by itself.
chunks.st: This teruma in abeyance should be burned by itself, and that impure teruma should be burned by itself;

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: and Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: both of them together.
chunks.st: In that case, both of them may be burned as one.

mishnayos.summary: As long as we may eat chametz, we may also feed it to animals or sell it. After that time, we may not use it at all. Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages argue how to get rid of it.

chunks.en: The whole time that we may eat chametz,
chunks.st: For the entire time that it is permitted to eat leavened bread,

chunks.en: we may feed it to animals, wild animals and birds,
chunks.st: one may also feed it to his domesticated animals, to non-domesticated animals, and to birds;

chunks.en: and sell it to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: and one may sell it to a gentile;

chunks.en: and we may get use from it.
chunks.st: and it is permitted to derive benefit from it.

chunks.en: Once its time has passed,
chunks.st: After its time passes,

chunks.en: we may not get any use from it,
chunks.st: it is prohibited to derive benefit from it,

chunks.en: and he may not even light an oven or a stove with it.
chunks.st: and one may not even light an oven or a stove with leavened bread.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: With regard to the manner of removal of leavened bread, Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the only way to get rid of chametz is by burning it.
chunks.st: The removal of leavened bread is to be accomplished only through burning.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he may also crumble it and throw it into the wind,
chunks.st: Burning is not required, as one may even crumble it and throw it into the wind

chunks.en: or throw it into the sea.
chunks.st: or cast it into the sea.

mishnayos.summary: Chametz that belonged to a non-Jew during Pesach may be used after Pesach, but chametz that belonged to a Jew during Pesach may not.

chunks.he: חָמֵץ שֶׁל נָכְרִי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו הַפֶּסַח,
chunks.en: Chametz of a non-Jew that was kept over Pesach
chunks.st: It is permitted for a Jew to derive benefit from leavened bread of a gentile

chunks.en: may be used after Pesach.
chunks.st: over which Passover has elapsed,
chunks.stMore: i.e., leavened bread that remains after the conclusion of Passover.

chunks.en: But chametz of a Jew
chunks.st: However, it is prohibited to derive benefit from leaven of a Jew

chunks.en: may not be used,
chunks.st: over which Passover has elapsed,

chunks.en: because it says: It shall not
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And no leavened bread shall be seen with you,

chunks.en: be seen with you, any leaven.
chunks.st: neither shall there be leaven seen with you, in all your borders” (Exodus 13:7).

mishnayos.summary: If a Jew gave chametz to a non-Jew as a pledge for a loan, or the other way around, this mishnah teaches if the chametz may be used after Pesach. It also teaches about chametz that got buried under fallen rocks.

chunks.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
chunks.en: A non-Jew who lent money to a Jew, with the Jew's chametz as a pledge:
chunks.explain: The Jew gave his chametz to the non-Jew to hold until he paid back.
chunks.st: If a gentile lent money to a Jew, and the Jew gave him leavened bread as collateral until after Passover,

chunks.en: after Pesach it may be used.
chunks.st: and after Passover the gentile retains this leavened bread in lieu of payment, then one is permitted to derive benefit from this leavened bread.
chunks.stMore: Since the leavened bread was retained by the gentile based on the transfer that took place prior to Passover, the leavened bread is considered to have belonged to the gentile during Passover.

chunks.he: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת הַנָּכְרִי עַל חֲמֵצוֹ,
chunks.en: And a Jew who lent money to a non-Jew, with the non-Jew's chametz as a pledge:
chunks.st: Whereas if a Jew lent money to a gentile, and leavened bread was given as collateral during Passover in the same manner as in the previous case, then

chunks.en: after Pesach it may not be used.
chunks.st: after Passover it is forbidden to derive benefit from this leavened bread.
chunks.stMore: Since this leavened bread was considered to be in the Jew’s property during Passover, it is forbidden to derive benefit from it afterward.

chunks.en: Chametz that a pile of rocks fell on
chunks.st: Leavened bread upon which a rockslide has fallen

chunks.en: counts as if it was gotten rid of.
chunks.st: is considered as though it has been eliminated, and it is not necessary to dig it up in order to burn it.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו:
chunks.en: it must be covered so deep that a dog can't dig for it.
chunks.st: Any leavened bread that has been covered to such an extent that a dog cannot search after it is considered to have been eliminated.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who eats terumah that is chametz on Pesach by mistake must pay the Kohen back. If he did it on purpose, he does not pay.

chunks.en: Someone who eats terumah that is chametz on Pesach by mistake
chunks.st: If one unwittingly eats teruma of leavened bread on Passover, not realizing that the food was teruma, then

chunks.en: pays the main amount plus a fifth more.
chunks.explain: This is what someone pays for eating terumah by mistake.
chunks.st: he must pay the principal and an additional fifth.
chunks.stMore: This is because one who unwittingly eats teruma must compensate the priest for the value of the teruma and add a fifth of the value, even though the teruma is considered to be valueless on Passover. If he

words.note: One fifth more than the main amount.

chunks.en: If on purpose, he does not have to pay, not even its worth as firewood.
chunks.explain: He gets a harsher punishment instead, and chametz on Pesach is worth nothing.
chunks.st: intentionally ate the teruma then he is exempt from payment; as he is liable to receive the severe punishment of karet, he is therefore exempt from the lesser punishment of payment. If he ate impure teruma in this manner then he is not even required to pay its monetary value in wood, for one who derives benefit from impure teruma calculates its value by treating it as though it were fuel for burning. While impure teruma can be used in this manner during the rest of the year, one may not derive any benefit from leavened bread on Passover, and therefore such teruma is worthless.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the five grains we may use for matzah on Pesach, and which kinds of matzah work for the mitzvah and which do not.

chunks.en: These are the things that a person fulfills
chunks.st: These are the types of grain

chunks.en: his duty with on Pesach:
chunks.st: with which a person fulfills his obligation to eat matza on the first night of Passover:

chunks.en: wheat and barley,
chunks.st: With wheat, with barley,

chunks.en: spelt, rye and oats.
chunks.st: with spelt [kusmin], with rye [shifon], and with oats [shibbolet shu’al].

words.note: Shibboles shual means fox-ear; it is the name of a grain like oats.

chunks.he: וְיוֹצְאִין בִּדְמַאי וּבְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
chunks.en: And one fulfills it with demai, and with maaser rishon that had its terumah taken,
chunks.st: And one fulfills his obligation by eating not only matza made from properly tithed grains, but even with matza made from doubtfully tithed produce, and matza made with first tithe from which its teruma was already taken, or

words.note: Food we are not sure had maaser taken from it.
The first tenth, given to the Leviim.

chunks.en: and with maaser sheni and hekdesh that were redeemed.
chunks.st: second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed.

words.note: A tenth that is eaten in Yerushalayim, or redeemed with money.
Things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And the Kohanim, with challah and terumah.
chunks.st: And priests may eat matza prepared from ḥalla, the portion of dough that is given to priests, or with teruma, as priests are permitted to eat these portions.

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: But not with tevel,
chunks.st: However, one may not fulfill one’s obligation to eat matza made with untithed produce,

words.note: Food that terumah and maaser were not yet taken from.

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְרוּמָתוֹ,
chunks.en: and not with maaser rishon that did not have its terumah taken,
chunks.st: nor with matza made from the first tithe from which its teruma was not separated,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
chunks.en: and not with maaser sheni and hekdesh that were not redeemed.
chunks.st: nor with matza made either from the second tithe, nor from consecrated grain that was not redeemed.

chunks.en: Loaves of a korban todah and wafers of a nazir:
chunks.st: With regard to one who prepared loaves of matza that are brought with a thanks-offering, or to the wafers brought by a nazirite, the Sages drew the following distinction:

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair for a while.

chunks.en: if he made them for himself,
chunks.st: If he prepared them for himself, then he

chunks.en: we don't fulfill the mitzvah with them.
chunks.st: does not fulfill his obligation to eat matza with them.

chunks.en: If he made them to sell in the market,
chunks.st: However, if he prepared them to sell them in the market to those who require these loaves or wafers,

chunks.en: we do fulfill the mitzvah with them.
chunks.st: one fulfills the obligation to eat matza with them.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the vegetables we may use for maror at the Seder, and how they may be prepared.

chunks.en: And these are the vegetables that a person fulfills
chunks.st: And these are the vegetables with which a person can

chunks.en: his duty with on Pesach:
chunks.st: fulfill his obligation to eat bitter herbs on Passover:

chunks.en: romaine lettuce, endives, horseradish, eryngo and maror.
chunks.st: One can fulfill his obligation with ḥazeret, with chervil [tamkha], and with field eryngo [ḥarḥavina], and with endives [olashin], and with maror.

words.note: Romaine lettuce.
Steinsaltz says chervil; many say horseradish.
A kind of thistle plant.
A bitter plant.

chunks.he: יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין,
chunks.en: We fulfill it with them whether fresh or dry,
chunks.st: One fulfills his obligation with them whether they are fresh or whether they are dry.

chunks.en: but not pickled, and not
chunks.st: However, one does not fulfill his obligation if they are pickled in water or vinegar, nor if they are

chunks.en: boiled too long, and not cooked.
chunks.st: over-boiled [shaluk] in hot water, nor if they are boiled [mevushal].

mishnayos.summary: On Pesach we may not soak bran or wheat in water, because it might become chametz.

chunks.en: We may not soak bran for chickens,
chunks.st: One may not soak coarse bran for feeding chickens, lest it be leavened.

chunks.en: A woman may not soak
chunks.st: A woman may not soak coarse bran to

chunks.st: however, she may rub coarse bran on her dry skin.

chunks.st: Likewise, the Sages said: A person may not chew wheat

chunks.en: We may not put flour into
chunks.st: One may not add flour to

chunks.stMore: In both cases, the pungency of these foods might accelerate the leavening of the flour.

words.note: A sharp-tasting food made from fruit and spices.

chunks.en: And if he put it in,
chunks.st: And if one added flour to either of these, the mixture may

chunks.en: in liquids and not in fruit juices.

chunks.en: These are things we may not keep on Pesach:

chunks.st: And for possessing these one transgresses [overin] the prohibitions of: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found, on Passover,
chunks.stMore: although not all of them are considered food:

chunks.en: Babylonian kutach,
chunks.st: Babylonian kutaḥ, a dip with a sharp flavor that contains flour;

words.note: A sharp dip made with flour.

chunks.en: and Median beer,
chunks.st: Median beer;

words.note: From the land of Madai.

chunks.en: and Edomite vinegar,
chunks.st: Edomite vinegar;

chunks.en: and Egyptian zisom,

chunks.en: and the dyers' soup,
chunks.st: dyers’ broth [zoman];

chunks.en: and the bakers' dough,
chunks.st: bakers’ well-worked dough;

chunks.en: and the glue of the scribes.
chunks.st: and kolan of soferim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.st: If one possesses any substance that is derived from a type of grain that became leavened, although it is not actually bread,

chunks.en: one may not keep it on Pesach.
chunks.st: one transgresses the prohibitions of: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found, on Passover.

chunks.st: These substances are included in the warning, i.e., the biblical prohibition of possessing leaven,

chunks.en: but they do not have the punishment of kares.

words.note: A very harsh punishment from Hashem.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about bits of dough stuck in the cracks of a kneading bowl, and about dough that we can't tell if it became chametz.

chunks.en: Dough in the cracks of a kneading bowl:
chunks.st: With regard to dough that is in the cracks of a kneading bowl,

words.en: that is in the cracks of

chunks.en: if there is a kezayis in one place,
chunks.st: if there is an olive-bulk of dough in one place, one

chunks.en: he must get rid of it.
chunks.st: is obligated to remove it.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if the dough does not add up to this amount,

chunks.en: it doesn't count, because it is so little.
chunks.st: it is nullified due to its insignificance.

chunks.en: And the same for the laws of tumah:
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to the halakhot of immersion to purify the bowl from ritual impurity,

chunks.en: if he cares about the dough,
chunks.explain: He plans to take it out.
chunks.st: if one is particular about the dough that is stuck in the cracks and he plans to remove it and use it,

chunks.en: it blocks the water of the mikvah. And if he wants it to stay,
chunks.st: it is a foreign substance that interposes between the kneading bowl and the water of the ritual bath, and invalidates the immersion of the bowl, leaving it ritually impure. And if he wants the dough to remain in place,

chunks.en: it counts like the bowl itself.
chunks.st: its status is like that of the kneading bowl itself and is not an interposition.

chunks.en: "Deaf dough,"
chunks.explain: Dough where we can't tell if it became chametz.
chunks.st: Deaf dough
chunks.stMore: is dough for which it is difficult to determine if it has been leavened. It is comparable to a deaf-mute, who cannot communicate.

words.note: Dough where we can't tell if it rose.

chunks.en: if there is dough like it that became chametz,
chunks.st: If there is dough similar to it in that water was added to both at the same time, which became leavened,

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.st: the deaf dough is prohibited.
chunks.stMore: Although it has not shown external signs of becoming leavened, it can be presumed that the deaf dough has also become leavened.

mishnayos.summary: The Rabbis argue what a woman should do when the challah she separates from her dough on Yom Tov of Pesach is tamei.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד מַפְרִישִׁין חַלָּה בְטֻמְאָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: How do we separate challah that is tamei on Yom Tov?
chunks.explain: Tamei challah may not be eaten and must be burned.
chunks.st: How does one separate ḥalla in ritual impurity during the Festival day of Passover?
chunks.stMore: Ordinarily, one may separate ritually pure ḥalla from dough and give it to a priest immediately so that he may eat it. Ritually impure ḥalla is unfit for a priest and must be burned, yet it is prohibited to bake or burn anything that is not fit to be eaten during the Festival day. However, it is also prohibited to wait and burn it after the Festival day, since it will become leavened in the meantime.

words.note: On Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: A woman

chunks.he: לֹא תִקְרָא לָהּ שֵׁם עַד שֶׁתֵּאָפֶה.
chunks.en: she should not call it challah until it is baked.
chunks.st: should not designate it as ḥalla prior to baking; rather, she should refrain from doing so until it is baked.
chunks.stMore: In other words, she should wait until she has baked all of the dough, and there is no risk of it becoming leavened. Only then should she separate ḥalla from it. The portion of ḥalla may then be kept until after the Festival day, when it may be burned.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beseira says,
chunks.st: Ben Beteira says: She should separate the ḥalla before it is baked, and

chunks.en: she should put it in cold water.
chunks.st: place the dough in cold water so that it will not become leavened.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: This is not the chametz that we are warned
chunks.st: This is not the leavened bread about which we are warned with the prohibitions:

chunks.en: about with "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found."
chunks.explain: The challah does not really belong to her.
chunks.st: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found.
chunks.stMore: These prohibitions do not apply because the ḥalla does not actually belong to the owner of the dough; it is instead considered to be consecrated property.

chunks.en: Rather, she separates it and leaves it until evening,
chunks.st: Rather, she should separate the ḥalla and leave it until the evening;

chunks.en: and if it becomes chametz, it becomes chametz.
chunks.st: and if it becomes leavened, then it will become leavened, but this is of no concern.

mishnayos.summary: The Rabbis argue how women may bake matzah together without the dough becoming chametz.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: three women may knead together
chunks.st: Three women may knead their dough as one, meaning at one time,

chunks.en: and bake in one oven,
chunks.st: and bake the batches of dough in one oven,

chunks.en: one after the other.
chunks.st: one after the other,
chunks.stMore: and they need not be concerned that their dough will become leavened while they are waiting to use the oven.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: three women may work on dough together:
chunks.st: Three women may be engaged in preparing dough as one, in the following manner:

chunks.he: אַחַת לָשָׁה וְאַחַת עוֹרֶכֶת וְאַחַת אוֹפָה.
chunks.en: one kneads, one shapes, and one bakes.
chunks.st: One kneads her dough as another one arranges her own dough so it takes the form of matza, while another one bakes her dough.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Not all women, and not all
chunks.st: Not all women, not all

chunks.st: wood, and not all ovens are the same, and therefore no set rules should be established.

chunks.en: This is the rule:

chunks.en: if it starts to rise, she should wet it with cold water.
chunks.st: rise, she should spread cold water in which she immersed her hands, onto the dough, in order to stop the leavening process.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about dough at different stages of becoming chametz, and whether one who eats it gets kares.

chunks.en: Dough that just started to rise must be burned,
chunks.st: Dough at the beginning of the leavening process [siur], must be burned,

words.note: Dough that just started to become chametz.

chunks.en: but one who eats it is not punished.
chunks.st: but one who eats it is exempt from the punishment of karet
chunks.stMore: because the dough had not become fully leavened.

chunks.en: Dough with cracks must be burned,
chunks.st: Dough that has reached the stage of cracking must be burned,

chunks.en: and one who eats it gets kares.
chunks.st: and one who eats it intentionally is liable to receive karet,
chunks.stMore: as he has intentionally eaten leavened bread during Passover.

chunks.en: What is siur?
chunks.st: What is considered siur?

chunks.en: When it has cracks like the feelers of grasshoppers.
chunks.st: Dough that has been leavened to the point that it has cracks that look like the antennae of locusts.

words.note: Thin feelers on a grasshopper's head.

chunks.en: "Cracked" is when its cracks have mixed into each other.
chunks.st: The stage of cracking occurs later in the leavening process, when the cracks intermingle.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: for both this and that,
chunks.st: One who intentionally eats either this or that, dough with cracks like locust antennae or with cracks that have become intermingled,

chunks.en: one who eats it gets kares.
chunks.st: is liable to receive karet,
chunks.stMore: as once dough begins to crack it has certainly become leavened.

chunks.en: And what is siur?
chunks.st: And what is siur?

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁהִכְסִיפוּ פָנָיו כְּאָדָם שֶׁעָמְדוּ שַׂעֲרוֹתָיו:
chunks.en: When its top turns pale, like a person whose hair stands up from fear.
chunks.st: It is any dough whose surface has becomes pale like the face of a person whose hair stands on end due to fear.

mishnayos.summary: When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbos, the Rabbis argue when we get rid of the chametz.

chunks.en: When the fourteenth of Nisan falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: With regard to the fourteenth of Nisan that occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: we get rid of all of it before Shabbos.
chunks.st: one removes all leaven from his possession, whether it is teruma or non-sacred food, before Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: except for that which will be eaten during the first part of Shabbat. In that case, one cannot remove leaven from his possession on the fourteenth of Nisan itself as he does in other years.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: One may remove the leaven

chunks.he: בִּזְמַנָּן. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: at its usual time. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says,
chunks.st: at its usual time on the fourteenth of Nisan by throwing it away or declaring it ownerless. Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says:

chunks.en: terumah before Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Only Kohanim may eat terumah, so it might not get finished on Shabbos.
chunks.st: Teruma should be removed before Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: as only a few people are permitted to eat it and therefore one can presume that it will remain uneaten during Shabbat.

chunks.en: and regular food at its usual time.
chunks.st: However, non-sacred foods should be removed at their usual time, on the fourteenth of Nisan itself.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who is on his way to do a mitzvah and remembers he has chametz at home: this mishnah teaches when he should go back to get rid of it, and when it is enough to cancel it in his heart.

chunks.en: One who is going to shecht his korban Pesach,
chunks.st: One who is traveling on the eve of Passover to slaughter his Paschal lamb,

words.note: To slaughter an animal the way the Torah says.

chunks.en: or to give his son a bris,
chunks.st: to circumcise his son,

chunks.en: or to eat an engagement meal in his father-in-law's house,
chunks.st: or to eat a betrothal feast in his father-in-law’s house,

chunks.he: וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ חָמֵץ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
chunks.en: and he remembers that he has chametz in his house:
chunks.st: and he remembers that he has leavened bread in his house,

chunks.he: אִם יָכוֹל לַחֲזֹר וּלְבַעֵר וְלַחֲזֹר לְמִצְוָתוֹ,
chunks.en: if he can go back and get rid of it and go back to his mitzvah,
chunks.st: if he is able to return to his house and remove the leaven and afterward return to the mitzva toward which he was traveling,

chunks.en: he should go back and get rid of it.
chunks.st: he should return home and remove his leaven.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: But if there is not enough time for him to go home and remove the leaven,
chunks.stMore: and still complete the mitzva that he already began,

chunks.en: he cancels it in his heart.
chunks.explain: He decides that it is like dust and he does not want it.
chunks.st: he should nullify it in his heart,
chunks.stMore: as by Torah law this is sufficient.

chunks.en: If he is going to save people from non-Jews,
chunks.st: If one was traveling to save Jews from an attack by gentiles,

chunks.en: or from a river,
chunks.st: from a flooding river,

chunks.en: or from robbers,
chunks.st: from bandits,

chunks.en: or from a fire,
chunks.st: from a fire,

chunks.en: or from a fallen building,
chunks.st: or from a collapsed building, he should not even attempt to return, and instead

chunks.en: he cancels it in his heart.
chunks.st: he should nullify the leaven in his heart.
chunks.stMore: This applies even if he could remove his leaven and still return to his previous activity.

chunks.en: And if he went to set his Shabbos place just because he wanted to,
chunks.explain: This is for an eruv techumin, to walk farther on Shabbos.
chunks.st: If he went to establish his Shabbat residence in order to adjust his Shabbat limit for an optional purpose, rather than in order to fulfill a commandment,

words.note: Not for a mitzvah, just because he wants.

chunks.en: he should go back right away.
chunks.st: he should return immediately to remove his leaven.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who left Yerushalayim and remembered he had holy meat with him: this mishnah teaches where he must burn it, and how much meat or chametz is worth going back for.

chunks.en: And so too, one who left Yerushalayim and remembered
chunks.st: And so too, the same halakha applies to one who left Jerusalem and remembered that there was

chunks.en: that he has holy meat in his hand:

chunks.st: consecrated meat in his hand.
chunks.stMore: Meat that is taken out of Jerusalem becomes disqualified, and one is required to burn it in proximity to the Temple.

words.note: Meat of a korban.

chunks.en: if he passed Tzofim,
chunks.st: If he passed the area of Mount Scopus [Tzofim], beyond which one cannot see Jerusalem,

words.note: A hill from where you can last see Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: he burns it where he is.
chunks.st: he burns the meat at the site where he is located;

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if he has not traveled that far,

chunks.he: חוֹזֵר וְשׂוֹרְפוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
chunks.en: he goes back and burns it in front of the Beis HaMikdash with wood of the mizbeach.
chunks.st: he must return and burn it before the Temple with wood from the arrangement on the altar, which was designated for burning consecrated items that were disqualified.

words.note: The fire on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: And for how much must they go back?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: For how much leaven or consecrated meat is one required to return?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: for both this and that, an egg's size.
chunks.st: In both this case and that case, one must return for an egg-bulk.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: for both this and that, a kezayis.
chunks.st: In both this case and that case, one must return for an olive-bulk.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say that the amount depends on the case:

chunks.en: holy meat, a kezayis,
chunks.st: With regard to consecrated meat, he is required to return if he has an olive-bulk,

chunks.en: and chametz, an egg's size.
chunks.st: but in a case where he remembers that he has leavened bread, he required to return only for an egg-bulk.

mishnayos.summary: Some places had a custom to work on Erev Pesach until midday, and some did not. This mishnah teaches that everyone follows the custom of his place.

chunks.en: In a place where people are used to doing work
chunks.st: In a place where the people were accustomed to perform labor

chunks.en: on Erev Pesach until midday,
chunks.st: on Passover eve until midday,

chunks.en: we may work. In a place where they are used not to work,
chunks.st: one may do so on that day. In a place where the people were accustomed not to perform labor,

chunks.en: we may not work.
chunks.explain: Working on Erev Pesach is not forbidden by the Torah. It depends on the custom.
chunks.st: one may not do so.
chunks.stMore: The performance of labor on the eve of Passover is not prohibited by Torah law, but is dependent on local custom.

chunks.he: הַהוֹלֵךְ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין,
chunks.en: One who goes from a place where they work to a place where they don't work,
chunks.st: If one travels from a place where people perform labor on Passover eve to a place where people do not perform labor,

chunks.he: אוֹ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין,
chunks.en: or from a place where they don't work to a place where they work,
chunks.st: or from a place where people do not perform labor on Passover eve to a place where people perform labor,

chunks.en: we put on him the strict rules of the place he left
chunks.st: the Sages impose upon him the stringencies of both the place from which he left

chunks.en: and the strict rules of the place he went to.
chunks.explain: So in both cases he may not work.
chunks.st: and the stringencies of the place to which he went.
chunks.stMore: In both cases, he may not perform labor. The Sages stated a principle:

chunks.en: And a person should not act differently,
chunks.st: And a person may not deviate from the local custom,

chunks.en: because of arguments.
chunks.explain: If he acts differently from the people there, it can start a fight.
chunks.st: due to potential dispute.

mishnayos.summary: Shemittah fruit may be kept at home only while that kind of fruit is still in the fields. This mishnah teaches about someone who brings Shemittah fruit from one place to another.

chunks.en: In the same way,
chunks.st: Similarly,

chunks.en: one who brings Shemittah fruit from a place
chunks.st: one who transports Sabbatical Year produce from a place

words.note: The seventh year, when we do not work the fields.

chunks.en: where it is finished to a place where it is not finished,
chunks.explain: Finished means none of that fruit is left in the fields.
chunks.st: where a crop has ceased in the fields to a place where it has not yet ceased

chunks.he: אוֹ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא כָלוּ לְמָקוֹם שֶׁכָּלוּ,
chunks.en: or from a place where it is not finished to a place where it is finished,
chunks.st: or from a place where it has not yet ceased to a place where it has already ceased

chunks.en: must get rid of it.
chunks.explain: He follows the stricter of the two places.
chunks.st: is obligated to remove the produce from his possession,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the stringencies of both locations. It is permitted for homeowners to eat Sabbatical Year produce in their houses only as long as that species of fruit remains in the field as ownerless property. However, once that particular fruit is no longer available for animals in the fields, one is required to remove what remains of that species from his home. The statement in the mishna is referring to one who transported fruit from a location where it ceased in the fields to one where it did not, and vice versa.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says

chunks.en: they say to him,
chunks.st: that he need not remove the produce, as he can say to a local resident:

chunks.en: "Go out and bring some for yourself too!"
chunks.st: You, too, go out and bring this produce from a place where it remains in the field.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz says he can say this to the people there; Bartenura says we say it to him.

mishnayos.summary: Some places had a custom to sell sheep and goats to non-Jews, and some did not. But no one may sell big animals like cows to them.

chunks.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לִמְכֹּר בְּהֵמָה דַקָּה לַגּוֹיִם,
chunks.en: In a place where people are used to selling small animals to non-Jews,
chunks.st: In a place where the people were accustomed to sell small livestock to gentiles,

words.note: Like sheep and goats.

chunks.en: we may sell. In a place where they are used not to sell,
chunks.st: one may sell them. In a place where the people were not accustomed to sell them due to certain concerns and decrees,

chunks.en: we may not sell.
chunks.st: one may not sell them.

chunks.en: And in every place we may not sell
chunks.st: However, in every place, one may sell to gentiles

chunks.en: to them big animals,
chunks.st: neither large livestock, e.g., cows and camels,

words.note: Like cows and camels.

chunks.en: calves or young horses, whether healthy or hurt.
chunks.explain: The Rabbis worried the animal might end up working on Shabbos for its Jewish owner.
chunks.st: nor calves or foals, whether these animals are whole or damaged.
chunks.stMore: The Sages prohibited those sales due to the concern lest the transaction be voided or one side reconsider, creating retroactively a situation where a Jew’s animal performed labor for the gentile on Shabbat in violation of an explicit Torah prohibition.

words.note: Hurt so they can't work well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda allows a hurt one.
chunks.explain: A hurt animal can't do work.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda permits the sale of a damaged animal because it is incapable of performing labor.

chunks.en: Ben Beseira allows a horse.
chunks.explain: It is used for riding, which the Torah does not forbid on Shabbos.
chunks.st: Ben Beteira permits the sale of a horse for riding, because riding a horse on Shabbat is not prohibited by Torah law.

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos different local customs discussed in the first mishna in this chapter, this mishna discusses various halakhot with regard to which there are different customs.

mishnayos.summary: Some places had a custom to eat roasted meat on the Pesach night, or to light a lamp on Yom Kippur night, and some did not. Everyone follows the custom of his place.

chunks.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לֶאֱכֹל צָלִי בְלֵילֵי פְסָחִים,
chunks.en: In a place where people are used to eating roasted meat on the nights of Pesach,
chunks.explain: Even outside Yerushalayim, or after the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed.
chunks.st: In a place where people were accustomed to eat roasted meat on Passover evenings,
chunks.stMore: outside of Jerusalem or after the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: we may eat it. In a place where they are used not to eat it,
chunks.st: one may eat it. In a place where people were accustomed not to eat outside Jerusalem,

chunks.en: we may not eat it.
chunks.explain: It would look like eating the korban Pesach outside its place.
chunks.st: one may not eat it.
chunks.stMore: The mishna discusses additional differences between local customs.

chunks.en: In a place where people are used to lighting
chunks.st: In a place where people were accustomed to kindle

chunks.en: a lamp on the night of Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: a lamp in the house on Yom Kippur evenings,

chunks.en: we light. In a place where they are used not to light,
chunks.st: one kindles it. In a place where people were accustomed not to kindle a lamp,

chunks.en: we do not light.
chunks.st: one does not kindle it.

chunks.en: But we light in shuls and in batei midrash,
chunks.explain: Even where the custom is not to light at home.
chunks.st: However, even in a place where the custom is not to kindle lamps in houses, one kindles in synagogues and study halls, in deference to these places.

words.note: Shuls.

chunks.en: and in dark alleyways,
chunks.explain: So people will not get hurt.
chunks.st: Similarly, lamps should be kindled in dark alleyways, so people will not be hurt,

chunks.en: and next to sick people.
chunks.st: and next to the sick.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna cites another custom related to Passover.

mishnayos.summary: Some places had a custom to work on Tisha B'Av, and some did not. The mishnah also tells how the people of Yehuda and the Galil worked on Erev Pesach.

chunks.he: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְתִשְׁעָה בְאָב,
chunks.en: In a place where people are used to working on Tisha B'Av,
chunks.st: In a place where people were accustomed to perform labor on the Ninth of Av,

chunks.he: עוֹשִׂין. מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה,
chunks.en: we may work. In a place where they are used not to work,
chunks.st: one performs labor. In a place where people were accustomed not to perform labor,

chunks.en: we may not work.
chunks.st: one does not perform labor.

chunks.en: And in every place Torah scholars stop working.
chunks.explain: They are sad about the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: And in all places Torah scholars are idle and do not perform labor on the Ninth of Av, due to the mourning over the Temple’s destruction.

words.note: Torah scholars.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
chunks.en: a person should always act like a Torah scholar.
chunks.explain: He should not work on Tisha B'Av.
chunks.st: With regard to the Ninth of Av, a person should always conduct himself as a Torah scholar and refrain from performing labor.
chunks.stMore: Apropos the discussion of performing labor on Passover eve, differences in other customs were cited.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: in Yehuda they used to work
chunks.st: In Judea, people would perform labor

chunks.en: on Erev Pesach until midday,
chunks.st: on Passover eves until midday,

chunks.he: וּבַגָּלִיל לֹא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כָּל עִקָּר.
chunks.en: and in the Galil they did not work at all.
chunks.st: and in the Galilee people would not perform labor on Passover eve at all.

chunks.en: And at night, Beis Shammai forbid working,
chunks.explain: The night before Erev Pesach.
chunks.st: With regard to performing labor on the night before Passover eve, the night between the thirteenth and fourteenth of Nisan, Beit Shammai prohibit performing labor,

chunks.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה:
chunks.en: and Beis Hillel allow it until sunrise.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel permit doing so until sunrise.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna continues the previous discussion of customs.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about what work may be done on Erev Pesach before midday.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: any work that he started
chunks.st: With regard to any labor that one began

chunks.en: before the fourteenth,
chunks.st: before the fourteenth of Nisan,

words.note: The fourteenth of Nisan, Erev Pesach.

chunks.en: he may finish it on the fourteenth.
chunks.st: he may complete it on the fourteenth before midday.

chunks.en: But he should not begin it
chunks.st: However, one may not begin to perform that labor

chunks.en: from the start on the fourteenth,
chunks.st: from the outset on the fourteenth,

chunks.en: even if he could finish it.
chunks.st: even if he is able to complete it before midday.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: three kinds of workers may do work
chunks.st: The practitioners of only three crafts are permitted to perform labor

chunks.en: on Erev Pesach until midday,
chunks.st: until midday on Passover eve,

chunks.en: and they are:
chunks.st: and they are:

chunks.en: tailors, barbers, and launderers.
chunks.explain: Their work is needed for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: Tailors, barbers, and launderers,
chunks.stMore: whose work is needed for the Festival.

words.note: Who cut hair.
Who wash clothes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

chunks.en: also shoemakers.
chunks.st: Even shoemakers are permitted to work on the fourteenth.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about taking care of hens and animals, and bringing things to a craftsman, on Erev Pesach and Chol Hamoed.

chunks.en: We may put eggs under hens to sit on them on the fourteenth.
chunks.st: One may place eggs under hens on the fourteenth of Nisan so that the birds will brood until the eggs hatch.

chunks.en: And a hen that ran away,
chunks.st: And if a hen fled from brooding,

chunks.en: we may put it back in its place.
chunks.st: one may restore it to its place.

chunks.en: And if it died,
chunks.st: And if a brooding hen died,

chunks.en: we may put another one in its place.
chunks.st: one may place another in its stead.

chunks.he: גּוֹרְפִין מִתַּחַת רַגְלֵי בְהֵמָה בְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
chunks.en: We may sweep from under an animal's feet on the fourteenth,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may sweep dung from beneath the legs of an animal on the fourteenth of Nisan.

chunks.en: and on Chol Hamoed we may push it to the sides.
chunks.st: And during the intermediate days of the Festival one may clear it to the sides.

words.note: Chol Hamoed.

chunks.en: We may take and bring things to and from the craftsman's house,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may take vessels to the craftsman’s house for repair and bring others from there

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָם לְצֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד:
chunks.en: even if they are not needed for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: even though they are not for the purpose of the Festival.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna continues the discussion of the halakhot of Passover eve.

mishnayos.summary: The people of Yericho did six things differently. The Sages protested three of them and did not protest the other three.

chunks.en: The people of Yericho did six things.
chunks.st: Six actions were performed by the Jewish residents of Jericho, contrary to common practice.

chunks.en: About three, the Sages protested to them,
chunks.st: With regard to three, the Sages reprimanded them,

chunks.en: and about three, they did not protest.
chunks.st: and with regard to three, the Sages did not reprimand them.

chunks.en: These are the ones they did not protest:
chunks.st: And these are the ones with regard to which they did not reprimand them:

chunks.en: They grafted palm trees all day long,
chunks.explain: On Erev Pesach, all day long.
chunks.st: The residents of Jericho would graft palm trees the entire day on the fourteenth of Nisan;

chunks.en: and they "wrapped together" Shema,
chunks.explain: They said Shema without the usual pauses.
chunks.st: and they would bundle Shema, as explained in the Gemara;

chunks.en: and they cut and piled up grain before the Omer,
chunks.st: and they would harvest and pile grain before the omer offering

words.note: The korban of new barley on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.en: and they did not protest to them.
chunks.st: was brought.

chunks.en: And these are the ones they protested:
chunks.st: And these are the ones with regard to which the Sages reprimanded them:

chunks.en: they allowed the branches of hekdesh trees,
chunks.st: They would permit the use of consecrated branches of carob or sycamore trees.
chunks.stMore: This refers to trees whose branches were cut and consecrated for Temple upkeep, which subsequently sprouted new branches;

words.note: Belonging to the Beis Hamikdash.

chunks.en: and they ate fruit fallen under trees on Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Maybe the fruit fell on Shabbos, and then it may not be eaten.
chunks.st: and they would eat fallen fruit from beneath palm trees that shed fruit that had fallen on Shabbat;

chunks.en: and they gave pe'ah from vegetables,
chunks.explain: Vegetables do not need pe'ah.
chunks.st: and they would designate the produce in the corner for the poor in a field of vegetables, which is exempt from this obligation even by rabbinic law.

words.note: The corner of the field left for the poor.

chunks.en: and the Sages protested to them.
chunks.st: And the Sages reprimanded the people of Jericho for doing these three things.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues the discussion of the halakhot of Passover eve, along with other local customs.

mishnayos.summary: King Chizkiyahu did six things. The Sages agreed with three of them and did not agree with the other three.

chunks.en: King Chizkiyahu did six things.
chunks.st: The Sages taught: King Hezekiah performed six actions.

chunks.en: The Sages agreed with him about three,
chunks.st: With regard to three of them, the Sages of his generation conceded to him;

chunks.en: and about three they did not agree with him.
chunks.st: and with regard to three of them, the Sages did not concede to him.

chunks.en: He dragged his father's bones on
chunks.explain: His father Achaz was wicked, so he did not give him a king's honor.
chunks.st: Due to King Hezekiah’s father’s wickedness, he dragged the bones of his father Ahaz

chunks.en: a simple bed of ropes,
chunks.st: on a bier of ropes and did not afford him the respect due to a king,

chunks.en: and they agreed with him.
chunks.st: and the Sages conceded to him.

chunks.en: He crushed the copper snake,
chunks.explain: The snake Moshe made in the desert. People began to worship it.
chunks.st: He ground the copper snake that Moses fashioned in the desert because Israel worshipped it,

chunks.en: and they agreed with him.
chunks.st: and the Sages conceded to him.

chunks.en: He hid away the Book of Cures,
chunks.st: He suppressed the Book of Cures,

chunks.en: and they agreed with him.
chunks.st: and they conceded to him.

chunks.en: About three they did not agree with him:
chunks.st: And with regard to three actions, the Sages did not concede to him.

chunks.en: He cut off the doors of the Heichal
chunks.st: He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary

words.note: The holy building of the Beis Hamikdash.

chunks.en: and sent them to the king of Ashur,
chunks.st: and sent them to the King of Assyria,

chunks.en: and they did not agree with him.
chunks.st: and they did not concede to him because he thereby demeaned the Temple.

chunks.en: He closed up the waters of the upper Gichon,
chunks.st: He sealed the waters of the upper Gihon stream, diverting its water into the city by means of a tunnel,

words.note: A spring near Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and they did not agree with him.
chunks.st: and they did not concede to him,
chunks.stMore: because he harmed the local populace in the process and should have relied upon God (Me’iri).

chunks.en: He made a leap year by adding a month in Nisan,
chunks.explain: He added a second Adar when it was already time for Nisan.
chunks.st: He intercalated the year, delaying the advent of the month of Nisan during Nisan,

chunks.en: and they did not agree with him.
chunks.st: and they did not concede to him.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara explains that he declared the first of Nisan to be the thirtieth of Adar and only then intercalated the year (see II Chronicles 30:2).

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what time the afternoon korban tamid was brought on a regular day, and how it was moved earlier on Erev Pesach.

chunks.en: The tamid is shechted at eight and a half hours
chunks.explain: Hours of the day, counting from morning.
chunks.st: The daily afternoon offering is slaughtered at eight and a half hours of the day, which is two and a half hours after midday,

words.note: The korban brought every day, morning and afternoon.

chunks.en: and offered at nine and a half.
chunks.st: and is sacrificed, i.e., its offering on the altar is completed, at nine and a half hours of the day.

chunks.en: On Erev Pesach it is shechted at seven
chunks.explain: It is earlier, so there is time for the korban Pesach after it.
chunks.st: On the eves of Passover, when the Paschal lamb must be offered after the daily offering, the daily offering is sacrificed earlier; it is slaughtered at seven and a half hours

chunks.en: and a half, and offered at eight and a half,
chunks.st: and sacrificed at eight and a half hours,

chunks.en: whether on a weekday or on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whether it occurs during the week or on Shabbat.

chunks.he: חָל עֶרֶב פֶּסַח לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: If Erev Pesach falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Then the korban Pesach must be roasted before Shabbos.
chunks.st: If Passover eve occurs on Shabbat eve,
chunks.stMore: when the Paschal lamb must be offered even earlier to ensure that it will be roasted before the onset of Shabbat,

chunks.he: נִשְׁחָט בְּשֵׁשׁ וּמֶחֱצָה וְקָרֵב בְּשֶׁבַע וּמֶחֱצָה,
chunks.en: it is shechted at six and a half and offered at seven and a half,
chunks.st: the daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half hours and sacrificed at seven and a half hours,

chunks.en: and the korban Pesach comes after it.
chunks.st: and the Paschal lamb is offered thereafter.

mishnayos.summary: A korban Pesach must be brought for its own sake. If it is done for a different korban, even in part, it is not kosher.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that was shechted not for its own sake,
chunks.explain: He said he was shechting it as a different korban.
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb that the priest slaughtered not for its own purpose,
chunks.stMore: i.e., at the time of slaughter he said that his intent was to slaughter it as a different offering, e.g., a peace-offering or burnt-offering, rather than as a Paschal lamb;

words.note: For being a korban Pesach.

chunks.en: or he caught the blood, carried it, or threw it not for its own sake,
chunks.st: or if the priest received the blood, or carried the blood to the altar, or sprinkled the blood on the altar while saying that it was not for the purpose of the Paschal lamb;

words.note: Caught the blood in a bowl.
Threw the blood on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: or for its own sake and not for its own sake,
chunks.st: or if the priest performed the rites both for its own purpose and not for its own purpose;

chunks.en: or not for its own sake and for its own sake,
chunks.st: or not for its own purpose and for its own purpose;

chunks.en: it is not kosher. What is "for its own sake and not for its own sake"?
chunks.st: in all these cases, the Paschal lamb is disqualified. How does one perform the rites for its own purpose and not for its own purpose?

chunks.en: For a korban Pesach and for a shelamim.
chunks.st: It is in a case where the priest said that his intent is for the purpose of the Paschal lamb and for the purpose of a peace-offering.

words.note: A peace korban.

chunks.en: What is "not for its own sake and for its own sake"?
chunks.st: And how does one perform rites not for its own purpose and for its own purpose?

chunks.en: For a shelamim and for a korban Pesach.
chunks.st: It is in a case where the priest says that the offering is for the purpose of a peace-offering and for the purpose of a Paschal lamb.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches for whom the korban Pesach must be shechted, and at what time of day.

chunks.en: If he shechted it not for the people who will eat it, and not for those signed up for it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for people who cannot eat it or for those who did not register in advance to eat it,

words.note: People who signed up to eat this korban.

chunks.en: or for people without a bris, or for people who are tamei,
chunks.explain: The Torah does not let them eat the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered it for people who are uncircumcised or for those who are ritually impure, whom the Torah prohibits from eating the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. For those who will eat it and for those who won't,
chunks.st: it is disqualified. However, if one slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it;

chunks.en: for those signed up and for those not signed up,
chunks.st: for those who have registered for it and for those who have not registered for it;

chunks.en: for those with a bris and for those without,
chunks.st: for the circumcised and for the uncircumcised;

words.en: and for those without a bris

chunks.en: for those who are tamei and for those who are tahor,
chunks.st: for the ritually impure and for the ritually pure,

chunks.en: it is kosher. If he shechted it before midday,
chunks.explain: Only part of his plan was wrong, so it still counts.
chunks.st: it is valid, for a partially invalid intent does not disqualify the offering. If one slaughtered the Paschal lamb before midday

chunks.he: פָּסוּל, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות יב) בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם.
chunks.en: it is not kosher, because it says, "in the afternoon."
chunks.st: it is disqualified, as it is stated: “And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it in the afternoon” (Exodus 12:6).

words.note: In the afternoon.

chunks.en: If he shechted it before the tamid,
chunks.st: If he slaughtered it before the daily afternoon offering

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אֶחָד מְמָרֵס בְּדָמוֹ
chunks.en: it is kosher, as long as someone keeps stirring its blood
chunks.explain: So that the blood does not get thick.
chunks.st: it is valid, as long as another person stirs its blood in order to prevent it from congealing

chunks.en: until the blood of the tamid is thrown.
chunks.st: until the blood of the daily offering is sprinkled.

chunks.en: And if it was thrown first, it is kosher.
chunks.st: And if the blood of the Paschal lamb is sprinkled before the blood of the daily offering, it is nonetheless valid, as this change does not disqualify the offering.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah says not to shecht the korban Pesach while owning chametz. The Tanna'im argue which korbanos this mitzvah is about.

chunks.en: One who shechts the korban Pesach while he has chametz
chunks.explain: While he still owns chametz.
chunks.st: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread still in his possession

chunks.en: breaks a "do not" mitzvah.
chunks.st: violates a negative commandment,
chunks.stMore: as the Torah states: “You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the sacrifice of the festival of Passover be left until the morning” (Exodus 34:25).

words.note: A mitzvah that says not to do something.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: also the tamid.
chunks.st: Even one who slaughters the daily afternoon offering on Passover eve with leaven in his possession violates the commandment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: the korban Pesach on the fourteenth:
chunks.st: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth of Nisan

chunks.en: for its own sake, he is guilty,
chunks.st: for its own purpose with leaven in his possession is liable;

chunks.en: and not for its own sake, he is free.
chunks.st: but if he slaughtered it for a different purpose he is exempt.

chunks.en: And all other korbanos,
chunks.st: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover eve, when owning leaven is prohibited,

chunks.en: whether for their own sake or not for their own sake,
chunks.st: whether he slaughtered them for their own purpose or he slaughtered them for a different purpose,

chunks.en: he is free. And during the Moed,
chunks.st: he is exempt. And during the festival of Passover,

words.note: During Pesach itself.

chunks.en: for its own sake, he is free,
chunks.explain: It is not a kosher korban at this time, so it does not count.
chunks.st: if one slaughtered the Paschal lamb for its own purpose he is exempt.
chunks.stMore: Since a Paschal lamb that is slaughtered for its own purpose at an improper time is disqualified, it is not an offering at all and there is no violation of the commandment: “You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread.”

chunks.en: and not for its own sake, he is guilty.
chunks.st: However, if he slaughtered it for a different purpose and thereby validated the sacrifice as a peace-offering, he is liable for having sacrificed it with leaven in his possession.

chunks.en: And all other korbanos,
chunks.st: And for all other offerings that one slaughters on Passover, when it is prohibited to slaughter with leaven in one’s possession,

chunks.en: whether for their own sake or not for their own sake,

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that he shechted not for its own sake on Shabbos,
chunks.st: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered for a different purpose on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: not knowing that it is prohibited for him to do so, is disqualified, and

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas for it.
chunks.explain: He did forbidden work on Shabbos by mistake.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering for it
chunks.stMore: because he unwittingly performed a prohibited labor on Shabbat.

words.note: A korban for doing a sin by mistake.

chunks.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח,
chunks.en: And all other korbanos that he shechted as a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: As for all other offerings, such as a peace-offering, that one unwittingly slaughtered on Shabbat for the purpose of a Paschal offering,

chunks.en: if they can't be a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: if they were not fit for the Paschal offering, e.g., if they were female or cattle or more than a year old and clearly ineligible for the Paschal offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one. And if they can be,
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering. Because he did not fulfill the mitzva to bring a Paschal offering, his act of slaughter was therefore unnecessary. And if they were fit,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer nevertheless deems him liable to bring a sin-offering for his unwitting transgression.

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua says he does not.
chunks.explain: He meant to do a mitzvah, and he did do a mitzvah.
chunks.st: But Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him,
chunks.stMore: because he maintains that if someone intended to perform a mitzva, and despite his error he in fact performed a mitzva, he is not liable to bring a sin-offering. And in this case he performed a mitzva, because offerings that are sacrificed for a different purpose are still fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.he: מָה אִם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא מֻתָּר לִשְׁמוֹ,
chunks.en: if the korban Pesach, which may be shechted for its own sake,
chunks.st: If, with regard to the Paschal lamb, which is permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for its own purpose,

chunks.en: when he changed its name,
chunks.st: when one changed its purpose he is

chunks.en: he must bring one, other korbanos, which are forbidden even for their own sake,
chunks.explain: Other korbanos may not be shechted on Shabbos.
chunks.st: nevertheless liable, then, with regard to other offerings that are forbidden to be slaughtered on Shabbat even for their own purpose,

chunks.en: when he changed their name,
chunks.st: when one changed their purpose,

chunks.en: isn't it logical that he must bring one?
chunks.st: is it not right that he should be liable?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: No. If you say so about the korban Pesach,
chunks.st: No, this reasoning is faulty. If you say that one is liable to bring a sin-offering if he slaughtered a Paschal lamb for a different purpose, it is

chunks.en: that he changed it to something forbidden,
chunks.st: because he changed its purpose for something forbidden,
chunks.stMore: as the offering he intended it to be may not be slaughtered on Shabbat.

chunks.en: can you say so about other korbanos,
chunks.st: But can you necessarily say the same thing about other offerings that he slaughtered for the purpose of a Paschal offering

chunks.en: that he changed them to something allowed?
chunks.st: and thus changed their purpose for something that is permitted to be sacrificed on Shabbat?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: the korbanos of the community will prove it,
chunks.st: Let the communal offerings, such as the daily offering and the additional-offerings of Shabbat and the Festivals, prove the matter,

words.note: Like the tamid and the mussaf.

chunks.en: which may be shechted for their own sake,
chunks.st: for they are permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for their own purpose,

chunks.en: and one who shechts another korban for their sake
chunks.st: and nevertheless, one who unnecessarily slaughters a different offering for their purpose

chunks.en: must bring a chatas. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: is liable.This indicates that even when a particular offering may be slaughtered, one is nevertheless liable if he slaughtered a different offering for the purpose of the permitted offering. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: No. If you say so about the korbanos of the community,
chunks.st: No, if you say this halakha with regard to communal offerings,

chunks.en: which have a set number,
chunks.st: it is because they have a limit,
chunks.stMore: as there is a specific number of communal offerings that must be offered on any particular day and there is no reason one would mistakenly sacrifice extra offerings for this purpose.

chunks.en: can you say so about the korban Pesach, which has no set number?
chunks.st: But can you necessarily say the same thing about the Paschal lamb, which does not have a limit, making it more likely for someone to make a mistake?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵמוּרֵי צִבּוּר, פָּטוּר:
chunks.en: even one who shechts for the korbanos of the community is free.
chunks.st: According to Rabbi Yehoshua, even one who unwittingly slaughters other offerings for the purpose of communal offerings beyond their daily limit is exempt for the same reason, i.e., that he intended to fulfill a mitzva that is permitted on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when someone who shechted a korban Pesach on Shabbos, and it turned out not to be kosher, must bring a chatas.

chunks.en: If he shechted it not for those who will eat it and not for those signed up for it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered a Paschal lamb on Shabbat and mistakenly intended it for those who cannot eat it, such as sick or elderly people who are unable to eat the meat, or for those who did not register for it,

chunks.en: for people without a bris or for people who are tamei,
chunks.st: or for the sake of the uncircumcised or for those ritually impure,

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas. For those who will eat it and for those who won't,
chunks.st: the offering is disqualified and he is liable to bring a sin-offering for his unnecessary act of slaughter. If, however, he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it,

chunks.en: for those signed up and for those not signed up,
chunks.st: or for those who registered for it and for those who did not register for it,

chunks.en: for those with a bris and for those without,
chunks.st: or for the circumcised and for those who are uncircumcised,

words.en: and for those without a bris

chunks.en: for those who are tahor and for those who are tamei,
chunks.st: or for those who are ritually impure and those who are ritually pure,

chunks.en: he is free. If he shechted it and it turned out to have a mum,
chunks.explain: The korban is still kosher, so his shechting was allowed.
chunks.st: he is exempt. Since a Paschal lamb slaughtered with dual intentions of these types is valid, the act of slaughter was justified. If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a blemish, the offering is disqualified, and

words.note: A flaw that makes an animal unfit for a korban.

chunks.en: he must bring one. If he shechted it and it turned out to be a hidden tereifah,
chunks.explain: He should have checked the animal for a mum first.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering for having unwittingly performed a prohibited labor on Shabbat, as he should have examined the animal before it was slaughtered. If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a hidden condition that would cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa] and that could not have been discovered before the slaughter even if it were examined properly, the offering is disqualified, but

words.note: An animal with a sickness that makes it not kosher.

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. שְׁחָטוֹ וְנוֹדַע שֶׁמָּשְׁכוּ הַבְּעָלִים אֶת יָדָם,
chunks.en: he is free. If he shechted it and then found out that the owners had pulled out,
chunks.explain: Nobody could have known about the hidden sickness.
chunks.st: he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering. This is not a case of shogeg, unwitting violation of Shabbat, but rather of ones, an unavoidable accident. If he slaughtered it and afterward it became known that the owners had withdrawn from it and registered for a different Paschal lamb, in which case this one was slaughtered unnecessarily, as no one was registered for it,

chunks.en: or that they died or became tamei,
chunks.st: or it became known that they had died or became ritually impure,

chunks.en: he is free, because he shechted with permission.
chunks.st: in all these cases he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering, because he slaughtered with permission.
chunks.stMore: At the time of the slaughter, he did not know and had no reason to suspect that the offering would be disqualified.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues with another halakha with regard to the Paschal lamb:

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and Rabbi Akiva argue how to roast the korban Pesach, and where to put its legs and insides.

chunks.en: How do we roast the korban Pesach?
We bring a spit made of pomegranate wood,

words.note: A long stick to hold meat over a fire.

chunks.he: תּוֹחֲבוֹ מִתּוֹךְ פִּיו עַד בֵּית נְקוּבָתוֹ,
chunks.en: push it in through its mouth all the way through it,
and he puts its legs and
