its insides inside it.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
Rabbi Akiva says,
this is like a kind of cooking,
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach must be roasted, not cooked.

chunks.en: rather, we hang them outside it.

mishnayos.summary: The korban Pesach must be roasted only by the fire itself. This mishnah teaches what to do if part of it touched the oven or its juice dripped.

chunks.en: We do not roast the korban Pesach
chunks.st: One may not roast the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: on a metal spit or on a metal grill.
chunks.st: on the metal spit nor on a metal grill [askela].

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok said,
chunks.st: However, Rabbi Tzadok said:

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁאָמַר לְטָבִי עַבְדּוֹ,
chunks.en: once Rabban Gamliel said to his servant Tavi,
chunks.st: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said to his slave Tavi:

chunks.en: "Go and roast for us
chunks.st: Go and roast

chunks.en: the korban Pesach on the grill."
chunks.st: the Paschal lamb for us on the grill.

chunks.en: If it touched the clay of the oven,
chunks.st: If the Paschal lamb touched the earthenware surface of an oven,

chunks.en: he must peel off that spot.
chunks.explain: That spot was roasted by the hot oven, not by the fire.
chunks.st: one must peel off its place on the Paschal lamb, as it was roasted by the heat of the oven and not by the fire itself.

chunks.he: נָטַף מֵרָטְבּוֹ עַל הַחֶרֶס וְחָזַר עָלָיו,
chunks.en: If some of its juice dripped on the clay and came back onto it,
chunks.st: If some of the gravy of the Paschal lamb dripped on the earthenware and then returned to it, i.e., the gravy splattered back onto the meat,

chunks.en: he must take off that spot.
chunks.st: one must remove its place.
chunks.stMore: Peeling off the outer layer is not enough, and one must remove some of the meat underneath the outer layer, because it is considered to have been cooked by the liquid rather than roasted by the fire.

chunks.en: If some of its juice dripped on the flour,
chunks.st: If some of the Paschal lamb’s gravy dripped onto hot flour,

chunks.en: he must take a handful from that spot.
chunks.st: one must remove a handful of flour from its place, i.e., the place where the gravy landed in the flour, and destroy it.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what to do if someone rubbed the korban Pesach with terumah oil or with oil of maaser sheni.

chunks.en: If he rubbed it with terumah oil,
chunks.st: In a case where one smears the Paschal lamb with teruma oil,

words.note: A gift for the Kohanim. Only they may eat it.

chunks.en: if it is a group of Kohanim,
chunks.st: if the Paschal lamb belongs to a group of priests

chunks.en: they may eat it. If they are Yisraelim,
chunks.st: they may eat it, as they are permitted to eat teruma. If the Paschal lamb belongs to a group of Israelites, then

chunks.en: if it is still raw,
chunks.st: if it is still raw,

chunks.en: he must rinse it. And if it is roasted,
chunks.st: one must rinse it in order to remove the teruma oil; and if it is roasted,

chunks.en: he must peel off the outside.
chunks.explain: The outside soaked up the terumah oil.
chunks.st: one must peel off the outer layer that has absorbed the oil, so that the Israelites do not eat the teruma, which is prohibited to them.

chunks.en: If he rubbed it with oil of maaser sheni,
chunks.st: If one smears the Paschal lamb with oil of the second tithe,

words.note: A tenth of the crops.
Second. It is eaten in Yerushalayim.

chunks.he: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂנּוּ דָמִים עַל בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה,
chunks.en: he may not make the people in his group pay for it,
chunks.st: he may not demand money for it from the members of the group,

chunks.en: because we do not redeem maaser sheni in Yerushalayim.
chunks.explain: In Yerushalayim it must be eaten, not sold.
chunks.st: as one may not redeem second tithe in Jerusalem.
chunks.stMore: Second-tithe produce that is in Jerusalem is meant to be eaten; it may be given as a gift to others, but may not be redeemed or sold.

mishnayos.summary: Some korbanos of the whole community may be brought even when they are tamei, but not eaten. The korban Pesach is different: it is eaten even when tamei.

chunks.en: Five things are brought even when tamei,
chunks.explain: When most of the people or Kohanim are tamei.
chunks.st: Five items, i.e., offerings, may be brought in a state of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: but they are not eaten when tamei.
chunks.st: but they may not be eaten in a state of ritual impurity.

chunks.en: The Omer, and the Two Loaves,
chunks.st: They are all communal offerings: The omer, which is brought in Nisan; the two loaves brought on Shavuot;

words.note: Brought on Shavuos.

chunks.en: and the Lechem Hapanim,
chunks.st: the shewbread, which were arranged each week;

words.note: The Lechem Hapanim on the Shulchan.

chunks.en: and the shelamim of the community,
chunks.st: the communal peace-offerings, which were brought on Shavuot;

chunks.en: and the goats of Rosh Chodesh.
chunks.st: and the goats sacrificed on the New Moons, which were sin-offerings eaten by the priests.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach that comes in tumah
chunks.st: However, the Paschal lamb that is sacrificed in impurity

chunks.en: is eaten in tumah,
chunks.st: is eaten even in impurity,

chunks.en: because from the start it comes only to be eaten.
chunks.st: as it is brought to begin with only for eating, which is the essence of the mitzva.
chunks.stMore: With regard to other offerings, the essence of their mitzva is fulfilled when they are sacrificed on the altar, and the eating is non-essential.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when the blood of a korban Pesach may still be thrown even though part of it became tamei.

chunks.en: If the meat became tamei and the fats are still fine,
chunks.st: If the meat of the Paschal lamb became ritually impure, and the fat remains pure and may be burned on the altar,

chunks.en: he does not throw the blood.
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach is mainly for eating.
chunks.st: one may not sprinkle the blood.

chunks.en: If the fats became tamei and the meat is still fine,
chunks.st: On the other hand, if the fat became impure and the meat remains pure,

chunks.en: he throws the blood.
chunks.st: one may sprinkle the blood because the meat remains fit to be eaten.
chunks.stMore: This is the halakha with regard to a Paschal lamb, whose primary purpose is to be eaten by those who have registered for it.

chunks.en: But with other korbanos it is not so,
chunks.st: However, with regard to other offerings it is not so.

chunks.en: rather, even
chunks.st: Rather, although

chunks.en: if the meat became tamei and the fats are still fine,
chunks.st: the meat has become impure and the fat remains pure,

chunks.en: he throws the blood.
chunks.st: one may sprinkle the blood, because part of the offering still remains valid.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when the korban Pesach is brought even in tumah, and when the people who are tamei must wait for Pesach Sheni.

chunks.en: If the whole community or most of it became tamei,
chunks.st: If the entire community or most of it became ritually impure,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים טְמֵאִים וְהַקָּהָל טְהוֹרִים,
chunks.en: or if the Kohanim were tamei and the community was tahor,
chunks.st: or the priests were all impure and the community was pure,

chunks.en: it should be done in tumah.
chunks.st: they should perform the ritual of the Paschal lamb in ritual impurity.

chunks.en: If a small part of the community became tamei,
chunks.st: If a minority of the community became impure, even if they are many people,

chunks.en: the tahor ones bring it on the first one,
chunks.st: those who are pure perform the ritual of the Paschal lamb on the first Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: and the tamei ones bring it on the second one.
chunks.st: and those who are impure perform the ritual on the second Pesaḥ.

words.note: Pesach Sheni, a month later.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen Gadol's tzitz helps fix some kinds of tumah after a korban was brought, but not others. This mishnah teaches which.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach whose blood was thrown,
chunks.st: In a case of a Paschal lamb whose blood was sprinkled

chunks.en: and afterwards we found out that it was tamei,
chunks.st: and subsequently it became known that the meat or blood was ritually impure,

chunks.en: the tzitz makes it accepted.
chunks.explain: The korban still counts.
chunks.st: the frontplate of the High Priest appeases God for the ritual impurity after the fact,
chunks.stMore: and the owners are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ.

words.note: The gold plate on the Kohen Gadol's forehead.

chunks.en: If the person's body was tamei,
chunks.st: If it became known later that the body of the individual who brought the Paschal lamb had become ritually impure,

chunks.en: the tzitz does not make it accepted,
chunks.explain: He must bring a korban on Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: the frontplate does not appease God.
chunks.stMore: The individual has not fulfilled his obligation to bring the Paschal lamb, and therefore he must observe the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: because they said,
chunks.st: This is because the Sages said that with regard to

chunks.en: for a nazir and for one who brings a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: the nazirite and one who performs the ritual of the Paschal lamb,

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine and more.

chunks.en: the tzitz makes up for tumah of the blood,
chunks.st: the frontplate appeases God for both impurity of the blood and meat of the offering,

chunks.he: וְאֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל טֻמְאַת הַגּוּף.
chunks.en: but the tzitz does not make up for tumah of the body.
chunks.st: but the frontplate does not appease God for impurity of the body of the individual bringing the offering.
chunks.stMore: The mishna introduces a halakha with regard to ritual impurity of the deep, a term that refers to a source of impurity that is unknown to anyone and is discovered only after it has rendered someone impure.

chunks.en: If he became tamei with "tumah of the deep,"
chunks.explain: Tumah that nobody knew about, like a hidden grave.
chunks.st: If it became known after the offering was brought that the person had become impure due to ritual impurity of the deep, e.g., if he was informed that there was a concealed grave under the place he had sat in a house where he had previously stayed,

chunks.en: the tzitz makes it accepted.
chunks.st: the frontplate appeases God and the offering is valid.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches where a korban Pesach that became tamei is burned, and with whose wood.

chunks.en: If all of it or most of it became tamei,
chunks.st: If the whole Paschal lamb or most of it became ritually impure,

chunks.he: שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי הַבִּירָה מֵעֲצֵי הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
chunks.en: we burn it in front of the Birah with wood from the mizbe'ach pile.
chunks.st: one burns it before the Temple [habira] with wood from the arrangement of wood on the altar that was given to the owners of the Paschal lamb for this purpose.

words.note: The Beis Hamikdash.
The wood set up on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: If a small part of it became tamei,
chunks.st: If a minority of it became impure,

chunks.en: and the leftovers, they burn it in their courtyards or
chunks.st: and similarly, with regard to the parts of the Paschal lamb that are leftover, which must be burned, the owners of the Paschal lamb burn it in their courtyards or

chunks.en: on their roofs, with their own wood.
chunks.st: on their roofs, with their own wood.

chunks.en: Stingy people burn it in front of the Birah,
chunks.st: Only the miserly, who want to save the expenditure of wood, burn it before the Temple

chunks.en: so they can use the wood of the mizbe'ach pile.
chunks.st: in order to benefit from the wood of the arrangement.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when a korban Pesach that cannot be eaten is burned right away, and when it must wait.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that went out of its place or became tamei
chunks.explain: It left the place where it may be eaten.
chunks.st: A Paschal lamb that was taken out of its permissible area or that became ritually impure

chunks.en: should be burned right away.
chunks.st: should be burned immediately on the eve of Passover.

chunks.en: If the owners became tamei or died,
chunks.st: If the owners became ritually impure or died,

chunks.en: it must wait until it spoils, and be burned on the sixteenth.
chunks.st: its form must be allowed to decay by leaving it for a period of time instead of burning it immediately, and it should be burned on the sixteenth of Nisan, immediately after the first day of the Festival.

words.note: Left until it is spoiled.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

chunks.en: this too should be burned right away,
chunks.st: This, too, should be burned immediately,

chunks.en: because it has no one to eat it.
chunks.st: because it has no one to eat it, which is also so severe a disqualification that decay of form is not required.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when the bones, sinews and leftovers of the korban Pesach are burned.

chunks.en: The bones and the sinews
chunks.st: The bones of the Paschal lamb that contain edible marrow but cannot be eaten because it is prohibited to break the bones of the Paschal lamb; and the sinews;

words.note: The strong strings in the meat.

chunks.en: and the leftovers should be burned on the sixteenth.
chunks.st: and the leftover meat should all be burned on the sixteenth of Nisan, immediately after the first day of the Festival.

chunks.en: If the sixteenth falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the sixteenth occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: they should be burned on the seventeenth,
chunks.st: they should be burned on the seventeenth,

chunks.en: because burning them does not push aside
chunks.st: because the mitzva to burn them does not override

chunks.en: Shabbos or Yom Tov.
chunks.st: Shabbat or the Festival.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, they are burned on the first weekday.

words.note: Yom Tov.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches which parts of the korban Pesach count as meat, and the punishment for breaking its bones.

chunks.en: Anything that is eaten in a big ox
chunks.st: Anything that is fit to be eaten in an adult ox, whose bones have fully hardened,

chunks.en: may be eaten in a soft young goat,
chunks.st: may be eaten in a young kid.
chunks.stMore: One may register for a Paschal offering in order to eat any of these parts, and eating any such part is considered a fulfillment of the mitzva to eat the Paschal lamb. However, any part of the animal that is inedible in an adult ox is not considered meat, even if it is soft enough to be eaten in a young kid. One may not register for a Paschal offering in order to eat one of these parts, and eating it is not a fulfillment of the mitzva to eat the Paschal lamb.

words.note: Young, with soft bones.

chunks.en: and the tips of the bones and the soft gristle.
chunks.st: And the soft ends of the ribs and the cartilage are soft enough to be considered edible and may therefore be eaten from the Paschal lamb.

words.note: The soft ends of the ribs.

chunks.en: One who breaks a bone of a tahor korban Pesach
chunks.st: One who breaks the bone of a Paschal lamb that is ritually pure

chunks.en: gets forty lashes.
chunks.explain: The Torah says not to break its bones.
chunks.st: receives forty lashes for having violated a prohibition stated in the Torah.

words.note: Malkus.

chunks.en: But one who leaves over from a tahor one, or breaks a bone of a tamei one,
chunks.st: But one who leaves over part of a ritually pure Paschal lamb and one who breaks the bone of a ritually impure Paschal lamb

chunks.en: does not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: do not receive forty lashes.

mishnayos.summary: If part of the korban Pesach went out of its place, that part must be cut off without breaking the bone. This mishnah also teaches what counts as inside and outside.

chunks.en: A limb that partly went out,
chunks.st: If a portion of a limb has gone out of its permissible boundary,

chunks.en: he cuts until he reaches the bone,
chunks.st: one must cut the meat until one reaches the bone at the point that separates between the part of the limb that went out of its boundary and the part that did not,

chunks.en: and he peels until he reaches the joint,
chunks.st: and then peel the meat away from the bone until one reaches the joint,

chunks.en: and he cuts there. And with other korbanos, he chops with a cleaver,
chunks.st: and cut off the limb at the joint, as it is prohibited to break the bone itself. And with regard to other offerings, one may chop off the part that exited with a hatchet,

chunks.en: because breaking their bones is not forbidden.
chunks.st: as it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

chunks.en: From the doorway inward counts as inside,
chunks.st: How does one determine the outer boundaries of a particular location? Anything that is located from the inside of the doorway inward is considered as though it is inside,

chunks.en: from the doorway outward counts as outside.
chunks.st: and anything that is located from the doorway outward is considered as though it is outside.

chunks.en: The windows and the thickness of the wall count as inside.
chunks.st: And the windows in the wall and the thickness of the wall are considered as though they are inside,
chunks.stMore: such that an offering is considered to have exited the premises only if it is taken outside the wall.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how two groups can eat their korbanos Pesach in the same house without mixing.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלוֹת בְּבַיִת אֶחָד,
chunks.en: Two groups that were eating in one house:
chunks.st: Two groups that were eating one Paschal lamb in one house
chunks.stMore: need not be concerned that they will appear to be one group.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין,
chunks.en: these turn their faces this way and eat,
chunks.st: Rather, these turn their faces this way and eat,

chunks.he: וְאֵלּוּ הוֹפְכִין אֶת פְּנֵיהֶם הֵילָךְ וְאוֹכְלִין,
chunks.en: and these turn their faces that way and eat,
chunks.st: and these turn their faces that way and eat.

chunks.en: and the hot water pot is in the middle.
chunks.st: And it is permissible for them to have the boiler from which they pour hot water in the middle, so that the waiter can easily serve both groups.

chunks.en: And when the waiter gets up to pour,
chunks.st: When the attendant who is serving both groups gets up to pour for the group of which he is not a member,

chunks.he: קוֹפֵץ אֶת פִּיו וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו
chunks.en: he closes his mouth and turns his face
chunks.explain: So he does not eat with the other group.
chunks.st: he must close his mouth and turn his face so that he does not accidentally eat with the other group,

chunks.en: until he reaches his group and eats.
chunks.st: until he reaches his group again and eats with it.

chunks.en: And the kallah turns her face away and eats.
chunks.explain: She is shy to eat in front of people she does not know.
chunks.st: And the bride, who is embarrassed to eat in the presence of men she does not know, turns her face away from her group and eats, although this may make it seem as though she is part of a different group.

words.note: A bride.

mishnayos.summary: When two people shechted a korban Pesach for the same person, whose korban does he eat from? This mishnah teaches about a wife, an orphan, and a servant.

chunks.en: A woman, while she lives in her husband's house,
chunks.st: A woman, when she is living in her husband’s house,

chunks.he: שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ,
chunks.en: if her husband shechted for her and her father shechted for her,
chunks.st: if her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf,

chunks.en: she should eat from her husband's.
chunks.explain: We assume she wants to be in her husband's group.
chunks.st: she should eat from her husband’s lamb
chunks.stMore: because it is assumed that the wife intended to be included in her husband’s group.

chunks.he: הָלְכָה רֶגֶל רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
chunks.en: If she went on the first Yom Tov to spend it in her father's house,
chunks.st: However, if, as was often customary, she went on the first Festival following her marriage to observe the Festival in her father’s house,

words.note: The first Yom Tov after her wedding.

chunks.he: שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ,
chunks.en: and her father shechted for her and her husband shechted for her,
chunks.st: then, if both her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf,

chunks.en: she may eat in the place she wants.
chunks.st: she may eat in whichever place she wishes,
chunks.stMore: since it is not obvious with whose group she intended to be included.

chunks.en: An orphan whose guardians shechted for him,
chunks.st: In the case of an orphan with multiple guardians, if each of his guardians [apotropsin] slaughtered a Paschal lamb on his behalf, intending that he be included in their group,

words.note: Grown-ups who take care of an orphan.

chunks.en: may eat in the place he wants.
chunks.st: he may eat in whichever place he wishes.

chunks.en: A servant of two partners
chunks.st: A slave jointly owned by two partners

chunks.en: may not eat from either of theirs.
chunks.explain: Unless they agreed first whose korban he will eat from.
chunks.st: may not eat from the lamb of either of them,
chunks.stMore: unless it was stipulated beforehand from whose lamb he will partake.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: One who is half a servant and half free,
chunks.st: One who is half slave and half free man

chunks.en: may not eat from his master's.
chunks.st: may not eat from his master’s lamb.
chunks.stMore: It is assumed that the master did not intend to allow this person’s free half to partake of the lamb, and therefore the master did not slaughter the lamb with him in mind. Consequently, the half slave is not included among those registered for his master’s offering unless he was explicitly included.

mishnayos.summary: A master sent his servant to shecht his korban Pesach. This mishnah teaches what happens if the servant forgot which animal the master asked for.

chunks.en: One who says to his servant,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his slave:

chunks.en: "Go and shecht the korban Pesach for me,"
chunks.st: Go and slaughter the Paschal offering on my behalf,
chunks.stMore: but does not specify which type of animal to slaughter, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: if he shechted a young goat,
chunks.st: If the slave slaughtered a kid,

chunks.en: he may eat it. If he shechted a lamb,
chunks.st: his master may eat it; if he slaughtered a lamb,

chunks.en: he may eat it. If he shechted a young goat and a lamb,
chunks.st: his master may eat it. If the slave slaughtered both a kid and a lamb,

chunks.en: he eats from the first one.
chunks.st: his master should eat from the first one that was slaughtered;
chunks.stMore: the second is invalid and should be burned.

chunks.en: If he forgot what his master told him,
chunks.st: If the master had stated explicitly which type of animal to slaughter, but the slave forgot what his master said to him,

chunks.en: what should he do?
chunks.st: what should he do?

chunks.en: He should shecht a lamb and a young goat and say,
chunks.st: He should slaughter both a lamb and a kid and say the following stipulation:

chunks.en: "If my master told me a young goat,
chunks.st: If my master said to me that I should slaughter a kid,

chunks.en: the young goat is his and the lamb is mine.
chunks.st: the kid is for his Paschal offering and the lamb is for mine;

chunks.en: And if my master told me a lamb,
chunks.st: and if my master said to me that I should slaughter a lamb,

chunks.en: the lamb is his and the young goat is mine."
chunks.st: the lamb is for his Paschal offering and the kid is for mine.
chunks.stMore: In this way, once the master ultimately clarifies what he had originally said, both animals may be used accordingly.

chunks.en: If his master forgot what he told him,
chunks.st: If his master also forgot what he said to him, neither animal may be used, since it has not been clarified which of the animals the slave and master are registered for.

chunks.en: both of them go out to the place of burning,
chunks.explain: Nobody knows whose korban each one is.
chunks.st: Therefore, both of them, the lamb and the kid, go out to the place designated for burning, in accordance with the halakha pertaining to offerings that may not be eaten.

chunks.en: and they do not need to bring a korban on Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: However, despite this, both the master and slave are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ if the blood of the animals has already been applied to the altar before the master forgot.

mishnayos.summary: A father promised the korban Pesach to whichever son reached Yerushalayim first. This mishnah also teaches until when people may join or leave a korban Pesach.

chunks.en: One who says to his sons,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his children:

chunks.en: "I am shechting the korban Pesach for
chunks.st: I am slaughtering the Paschal lamb on behalf of

chunks.en: whichever of you goes up first to Yerushalayim,"
chunks.st: whomever of you goes up first to Jerusalem,

chunks.en: once the first one brought in his head and most of his body,
chunks.st: as soon as the first of the children has entered his head and the majority of his body into Jerusalem,

chunks.he: זָכָה בְחֶלְקוֹ וּמְזַכֶּה אֶת אֶחָיו עִמּוֹ.
chunks.en: he gets his share and gets shares for his brothers with him.
chunks.explain: The father really wanted all of them to be in the group.
chunks.st: he has acquired his portion and acquires on behalf of his brothers their portions together with him.

chunks.en: People can always sign up for it, as long as there is
chunks.st: Additional people can always be registered for a Paschal lamb, as long as there will be

chunks.en: a kezayis of it for each and every one.
chunks.st: at least an olive-bulk of the lamb’s meat for each and every person registered.

chunks.en: People may sign up and pull out
chunks.st: People can be registered and withdraw themselves from being registered for a Paschal lamb

chunks.en: from it until it is shechted.
chunks.st: until it is slaughtered.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: until he throws its blood.
chunks.st: Even until the priest sprinkles the blood.

mishnayos.summary: Someone in a korban Pesach group added another person to his share. This mishnah teaches what the rest of the group may do.

chunks.en: One who signs up other people with him in his share,
chunks.st: If one who is registered for a Paschal lamb unilaterally registers another person with him in his portion of the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: the members of the group may give
chunks.st: the other members of his group are permitted to give him,

chunks.en: him his own share,
chunks.st: i.e., the one who included the additional person, only his portion, which was originally allotted to him.

chunks.en: and he eats from his,
chunks.st: And he, the additional person, eats from his portion, i.e., the portion of he who added him;

chunks.en: and they eat from theirs.
chunks.explain: They did not agree to add the new person.
chunks.st: and they, the other members of the group, eat from theirs.
chunks.stMore: This is because they did not agree to the inclusion of the additional person.

mishnayos.summary: People who had a kind of tumah and are becoming tahor: this mishnah teaches on which day a korban Pesach may already be shechted for them.

chunks.en: A zav who had it happen twice
chunks.explain: He must count seven clean days and go to the mikvah.

words.note: Someone with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: we shecht for him on his seventh day.
chunks.explain: By night he will be tahor and can eat it.

chunks.en: If he had it three times,
we shecht for him on his eighth day.
chunks.explain: On that day he brings his korban and becomes fully tahor.

chunks.en: A woman who waits one day for one day,

words.note: A woman with a kind of tumah who must wait one day.

chunks.en: we shecht for her on her second day.
If it happened two days,
we shecht for her on the third day.
And a zavah, we shecht for her on the eighth day.

words.note: A woman with a kind of tumah.

mishnayos.summary: We may shecht a korban Pesach for people who might not be able to eat it, but only together with others. This mishnah teaches who they are.

chunks.en: An onen, and one digging through a pile of fallen stones,
chunks.explain: Someone might be under the pile.
chunks.st: An acute mourner, i.e., a mourner on the day of the death of an immediate relative; and one clearing a pile of stones that collapsed on top of a person, in which case there is a possibility that the person buried underneath is dead and his corpse will impart ritual impurity to the person clearing the pile;

words.note: A mourner on the day a close relative died.

chunks.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהִבְטִיחוּהוּ לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים,
chunks.en: and so too one who was promised to be let out of prison,
chunks.st: and similarly, one whom the governing body promised to release from prison on the night of Passover;

chunks.he: וְהַחוֹלֶה וְהַזָּקֵן שֶׁהֵן יְכוֹלִין לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת,
chunks.en: and a sick person and an old person who can eat a kezayis,
chunks.st: and an ill person and an elderly person who are still capable of eating an olive-bulk of meat,

chunks.en: we shecht for them.
chunks.st: one slaughters the Paschal lamb on their behalf,
chunks.stMore: since they are currently fit to eat the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: But for all of them we do not shecht
chunks.st: However, with regard to all of them, this is only true when they are included in a group with other people who will definitely be able to partake of the lamb; but we do not slaughter the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: for them alone,
chunks.st: on their behalf if they are by themselves, either as individuals or in a group composed entirely of such people,

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא יָבִיאוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח לִידֵי פְסוּל.
chunks.en: in case they cause the korban Pesach to become unfit.
chunks.st: because perhaps they will cause the Paschal lamb to become disqualified,
chunks.stMore: since there is a possibility that by the night of Passover they will be unable to partake of the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: So if something happened that made them unfit,
chunks.st: Therefore, since they were registered for a Paschal lamb and it was slaughtered when they were still fit to partake of it, even if a disqualification occurred to them later, preventing them from partaking of the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: they do not need to bring Pesach Sheni,
chunks.explain: The korban was shechted for them when they were fit.
chunks.st: they are nevertheless exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ.
chunks.stMore: The exemption from the second Pesaḥ is dependent not on whether they partook of a Paschal lamb, but on whether it was validly slaughtered on their behalf.

chunks.en: except for the one digging through the pile,
chunks.explain: If the person under it had died.
chunks.st: This holds true except for one who was clearing a pile of stones where the person buried underneath was eventually found dead,

chunks.en: because he was tamei from the start.
chunks.st: because in such a case the person searching for him certainly stood over the corpse at some point. He had therefore become ritually impure from the outset, even before the Paschal lamb was slaughtered.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, he would not have been fit even during the slaughter and will have to observe the second Pesaḥ.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei argue whether a korban Pesach may be shechted for one person alone. The mishnah also teaches which groups may not be made.

chunks.he: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד,
chunks.en: We do not shecht the korban Pesach for one person alone.
chunks.st: We do not slaughter the Paschal lamb on behalf of an individual, only for a group of people;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yosei allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

chunks.en: Even a group of a hundred
chunks.st: And even if there is a group of one hundred

chunks.en: who can't eat a kezayis,
chunks.st: who together are unable to eat an olive-bulk of it,

chunks.en: we do not shecht for them.
chunks.st: we do not slaughter on their behalf.

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין חֲבוּרַת נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים:
chunks.en: And we do not make a group of women, servants and children.
chunks.st: And we do not make a group for a Paschal lamb that consists of women, slaves, and minors.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when an onen, and a ger who joined the Jewish people on Erev Pesach, may eat the korban Pesach.

chunks.he: אוֹנֵן טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב,
chunks.en: An onen goes to the mikvah and eats his korban Pesach at night,
chunks.explain: The Rabbis made an onen's mourning last into the night too, but not for the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: but not other korbanos.
One who hears about the death of his relative,
chunks.explain: He heard about it more than thirty days later.

chunks.en: and one who gathers bones for himself,
chunks.explain: Moving his parents' bones to their lasting kever.

chunks.en: goes to the mikvah and eats korbanos.
A ger who became a Jew on Erev Pesach,

words.note: Someone who joins the Jewish people.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
he goes to the mikvah and eats his korban Pesach at night.
And Beis Hillel say,

chunks.he: הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הָעָרְלָה כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַקָּבֶר:
chunks.en: one who leaves the state of not having a bris is like one who leaves a grave.
chunks.explain: He must wait seven days to become tahor, like someone who became tamei from a dead person.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who did not bring the korban Pesach on time brings it on Pesach Sheni, a month later. This mishnah teaches who must bring it, and why the Torah names only two kinds of people.

chunks.en: One who was tamei or on a far
chunks.st: One who was ritually impure or on a distant journey

chunks.en: journey, and did not bring the first one,
chunks.st: and did not observe the first Pesaḥ by participating in the offering of the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth of Nisan

chunks.en: should bring the second one.
chunks.st: should observe the second Pesaḥ by participating in the offering on the fourteenth of Iyyar.

words.note: Pesach Sheni, on the fourteenth of Iyar.

chunks.en: If he made a mistake or could not help it, and
chunks.st: If one unwittingly forgot or was prevented due to circumstances beyond his control and

chunks.en: did not bring the first one,
chunks.st: did not observe the first Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: he should bring the second one.
chunks.st: he too should observe the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If so, that the second Pesaḥ is observed even by someone who forgot or was prevented from observing the first Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: why does the Torah say "tamei" or
chunks.st: why is it stated in the Torah that the second Pesaḥ is observed only by one who was ritually impure

chunks.en: "who was on a far journey"?
chunks.st: or on a distant journey?

chunks.en: To teach that these do not get kares,
chunks.explain: If they do not bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: These cases were specified in order to teach that these two groups of people are exempt from karet if they do not observe the second Pesaḥ,

chunks.en: and these do get kares.
chunks.st: but those who were not ritually impure or on a distant journey are liable to receive karet, as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer argue what counts as a "far journey" for the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: What is a far journey?
chunks.st: What is the definition of a distant journey that exempts one from observing the first Pesaḥ?

chunks.en: From Modi'in and farther,
chunks.st: Anywhere from the city of Modi’im and beyond,

words.note: A town far from Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and the same distance in every direction.
chunks.st: and from anywhere located an equal distance from Jerusalem and beyond in every direction;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: from the doorstep of the Azarah and farther.
chunks.explain: Anyone outside the Azarah when the korban is shechted.
chunks.st: From the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond
chunks.stMore: is considered a distant journey;therefore, anyone located outside the courtyard at the time that the Paschal lamb is slaughtered is exempt from observing the first Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

chunks.en: that is why there is a dot on the letter hei,
chunks.explain: In the Torah, the word for "far" has a dot over its hei.
chunks.st: Therefore, the word is dotted over the letter heh in the word “distant [reḥoka]”

chunks.en: to say: not because it is really far,
chunks.st: to say that the meaning of the word should be qualified: It should be understood that it is not because he is really distant;

chunks.en: but from the doorstep of the Azarah and farther.
chunks.st: rather, it includes anyone located from the threshold of the Temple courtyard and beyond.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how the korban Pesach on Pesach Sheni is different from the first one, and how they are the same.

chunks.en: What is the difference between the first Pesach and the second?
chunks.st: What is the difference between the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ and the Paschal lamb offered on the second Pesaḥ?

chunks.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר בְּבַל יֵרָאֶה וּבַל יִמָּצֵא,
chunks.en: On the first, having chametz is forbidden because of "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found."
chunks.st: On the first Pesaḥ, at the time of slaughtering the Paschal lamb, it is prohibited to own leavened bread due to the prohibitions: It shall not be seen, and: It shall not be found.

chunks.en: And on the second, he may have matzah and chametz with him in the house.
chunks.st: And on the second Pesaḥ it is permissible for one to have both leavened bread and matza with him in the house.

chunks.en: The first needs Hallel while eating it,
chunks.st: Another difference is that the Paschal lamb offered on the first Pesaḥ requires the recitation of hallel as it is eaten

chunks.en: and the second does not need Hallel while eating it.
chunks.st: and the second does not require the recitation of hallel as it is eaten.

chunks.en: Both of them need Hallel while they are made,
chunks.explain: While the korbanos are shechted.
chunks.st: However, they are the same in that the Paschal lambs sacrificed on both the first and second Pesaḥ require the recitation of hallel as they are prepared, i.e., as they are slaughtered,

chunks.en: and they are eaten roasted with matzos and maror,
chunks.st: and they are both eaten roasted with matza and bitter herbs,

chunks.en: and they push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: and they override Shabbat in that they may be slaughtered and their blood sprinkled even on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: When the korban Pesach is brought while most people are tamei, people with other kinds of tumah still may not eat it. This mishnah teaches what happens if they did.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that comes in tumah,
chunks.explain: When most of the people are tamei from a dead person.

chunks.en: zavim may not eat from it,

words.note: People with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: nor zavos, niddos, or women who just had a baby.

words.note: Women with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: But if they ate,
they do not get kares.
Rabbi Eliezer frees them even
for going into the Beis Hamikdash.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how the korban Pesach in Mitzrayim was different from the korban Pesach of all later years.

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין פֶּסַח מִצְרַיִם לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת,
chunks.en: What is the difference between the Pesach of Mitzrayim and the Pesach of the generations?
chunks.st: What are the differences between the Paschal lamb that the Jewish people offered in Egypt and the Paschal lamb offered in all later generations?

chunks.en: The Pesach of Mitzrayim was taken on the tenth,
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb the Jewish people offered in Egypt had to be taken from the tenth of the month of Nisan

chunks.en: and it needed sprinkling with a bunch of hyssop on
chunks.st: and required the people to sprinkle its blood with a bundle of hyssop, unlike the Paschal lamb in all later years, and its blood was also sprinkled

words.note: A plant, eizov.

chunks.en: the top of the door and on the two doorposts,
chunks.st: upon the lintel and the two doorposts,

chunks.en: and it was eaten in a hurry, on one night.
chunks.st: and it was eaten with haste; in addition, the Paschal lamb in Egypt was only on one night,

chunks.en: But the Pesach of the generations lasts all seven days.
chunks.explain: No chametz is allowed all seven days.
chunks.st: whereas the Paschal lamb throughout the generations is observed for seven days.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua heard two different rules about an animal swapped for a korban Pesach, and Rabbi Akiva explains when each one is true.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: I heard that the swap of a korban Pesach is offered,
chunks.st: I heard two rulings from my teachers: One ruling was that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering after Passover,

words.note: An animal someone tried to swap for a korban. It also becomes holy.

chunks.en: and that the swap of a korban Pesach is not offered,
chunks.st: and another ruling was that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not sacrificed as a peace-offering after Passover;

chunks.en: and I can't explain it.
chunks.st: and I cannot explain these two rulings,
chunks.stMore: as I do not remember the circumstances to which each ruling applies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: I will explain.
chunks.st: I will explain:

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that was lost and found before the korban Pesach was shechted,
chunks.explain: He had already set aside another one in its place.
chunks.st: With regard to a lamb that is separated as a Paschal lamb and is then lost, leading the owner to separate another animal as its replacement, and is later found before the slaughter of the replacement Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it should graze until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: it is left to graze until it becomes unfit [yista’ev] and disqualified for use as a sacrifice.

chunks.en: and be sold, and he buys a shelamim with its money.
chunks.st: It is then sold and becomes unconsecrated, and the owner must bring a peace-offering with its proceeds.

chunks.en: And the same for its swap.
chunks.st: And so too, the same is true with regard to its substitute:
chunks.stMore: If one separates another lamb as a substitute for this replacement, the sanctity of the original lamb extends to the substitute as well. In the case outlined above, the substitute would graze, just like the replacement, until it developed a blemish and would then be sold. This is the circumstance in which the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not sacrificed.

chunks.en: After the korban Pesach was shechted,
chunks.st: On the other hand, if the lost lamb is found after the slaughter of the replacement Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: it is offered as a shelamim,
chunks.st: it itself is sacrificed as a peace-offering,

chunks.en: and the same for its swap.
chunks.st: and so too, its substitute is sacrificed, which explains the ruling that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what to do with an animal that cannot be a korban Pesach, and with a korban Pesach whose owner died.

chunks.en: One who sets aside a female for his korban Pesach, or
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach must be a male.
chunks.st: In the case of one who separates a female animal for his Paschal lamb although the Torah requires a male,

chunks.en: a male in its second year,
chunks.explain: It must be in its first year.
chunks.st: or a male that is in its second year although a Paschal lamb must be an animal that is in its first year,

chunks.en: it should graze until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: the animal is left to graze until it develops a blemish and becomes unfit,

chunks.en: and be sold, and its money goes for nedavah korbanos.
chunks.st: and it is then sold and its money is used for free-will offerings or peace-offerings.

words.note: Korbanos given just because one wants to.

chunks.en: One who set aside his korban Pesach and died,
chunks.st: With regard to one who separates his Paschal lamb and then dies,

chunks.he: לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ בְנוֹ אַחֲרָיו לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח,
chunks.en: his son after him should not bring it as a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: his son may not bring it after him for the purpose of a Paschal lamb because it may no longer be used for that purpose after its owner has died.

chunks.en: but as a shelamim.
chunks.st: Rather, it is brought for the purpose of a peace-offering.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what to do if a korban Pesach got mixed up with other korbanos, or with bechoros.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that got mixed up with other korbanos,
chunks.st: In the case of a Paschal lamb that was intermingled with other offerings,
chunks.stMore: such as guilt-offerings and burnt-offerings, and it is not known which animal was separated for which offering,

chunks.en: all of them should graze until they get a mum,
chunks.st: all of them are left to graze until they develop a blemish and become unfit;

chunks.he: וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
chunks.en: and be sold, and with the money of the best of them he brings one of this kind,
chunks.st: and they are then sold, and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this type of sacrifice,

chunks.en: and with the money of the best of them one of this kind,
chunks.explain: For each kind, he pays the price of the most expensive animal.
chunks.st: and with the proceeds of the choicest of them he must bring this other type of sacrifice,
chunks.stMore: meaning that he must purchase one of each type of sacrifice that was intermingled at the value of the most expensive animal in the group.

chunks.en: and he loses the extra from his own pocket.
chunks.st: And he loses the difference from his own pocket.
chunks.stMore: Not all the offerings were as expensive as the most valuable animal in the group, yet he must purchase an animal for each type of offering for the value of the most expensive animal in the group.

chunks.en: If it got mixed up with bechoros,
chunks.st: If a Paschal lamb was intermingled with firstborn animals,

words.note: Firstborn animals, given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: if they are a group of Kohanim, they may eat them.
chunks.st: If those whose offerings became mixed together were groups of priests, they may eat all of the animals on Passover night.
chunks.stMore: This is because priests are permitted to eat the meat of a firstborn animal, and the slaughter and other services for a firstborn animal are the same as those for a Paschal lamb. The attending priests should state that they intend to sacrifice as a Paschal lamb whichever animal is the Paschal lamb and to sacrifice as a firstborn animal whichever animal is a firstborn.

mishnayos.summary: A group's korban Pesach got lost and one of them went to look for it, while the others shechted a new one. This mishnah teaches who eats from which korban, depending on what they told each other.

chunks.en: A group whose korban Pesach got lost,
chunks.st: With regard to a group whose Paschal lamb was lost,

chunks.en: and they said to one of them,
chunks.st: and they said to one member of the group:

chunks.en: "Go and look for it, and shecht it for us,"
chunks.st: Go and search for our Paschal lamb, and when you find it, slaughter it on our behalf;

chunks.en: and he went and found it and shechted it,
chunks.st: and he went and found the missing offering and slaughtered it on behalf of the entire group,

chunks.en: and they took another one and shechted it:
chunks.st: but in the meantime they took a different animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: if his was shechted first,
chunks.st: If his Paschal lamb was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his offering, as he is considered to be registered specifically for that offering,

chunks.en: and they eat with him from his.
chunks.st: and they eat with him from his offering, because he included them in his offering and it belongs to the entire group.
chunks.stMore: The second animal does not have any registrants and is therefore burned.

chunks.en: And if theirs was shechted first,
chunks.st: And if theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs
chunks.stMore: because they withdrew from the original offering through the act of slaughtering a replacement,

chunks.en: and he eats from his.
chunks.st: and he eats from his because he was not registered for the replacement offering sacrificed by the remainder of his group.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of the offerings

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: or if both were shechted together,
chunks.st: or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his

chunks.en: and they do not eat with him,
chunks.st: and they do not eat with him in case theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: and theirs goes out to the place of burning,
chunks.st: and theirs must be taken out to the place designated for burning.
chunks.stMore: The offering slaughtered by the group may not be eaten due to the concern that it was slaughtered second and the members of the group would therefore have been included in the first offering.

chunks.en: and they do not need to bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: However, they are exempt from performing the offering of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ,
chunks.stMore: because they were included in the slaughter of whichever animal was slaughtered first. It is only due to external circumstances that they cannot complete the mitzva by eating the Paschal lamb, and this does not prevent them from fulfilling their obligation.

chunks.en: If he said to them,
chunks.st: A somewhat different case of a lost Paschal lamb would occur if the group had sent one member as an agent to search for the lost animal, and the agent said to the other members of the group before he left:

chunks.en: "If I am late,
chunks.st: If I am late,

chunks.en: go and shecht for me,"
chunks.st: go and slaughter a Paschal lamb for me.

chunks.en: and he went and found it,
chunks.st: He then went and found the lost Paschal lamb

chunks.en: and shechted it, and they took another one and shechted it:
chunks.st: and slaughtered it, and they took another animal and slaughtered it as a Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: if theirs was shechted first,
chunks.st: In that case, if theirs was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs

chunks.en: and he eats with them.
chunks.st: and he eats with them,
chunks.stMore: because he requested to be included in their offering and they registered him for their Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: And if his was shechted first,
chunks.st: And if his was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: he eats from his,
chunks.st: he eats from his

chunks.en: and they eat from theirs.
chunks.st: and they eat from theirs,
chunks.stMore: because the fact that they slaughtered a different animal indicates that they have withdrawn from the original offering.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of the animals

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: or if both were shechted together,
chunks.st: or if both the group and the individual slaughtered them together,

chunks.en: they eat from theirs,
chunks.st: they eat from theirs
chunks.stMore: because they definitely withdrew from the original offering by slaughtering a different one,

chunks.en: and he does not eat with them,
chunks.st: and he does not eat with them
chunks.stMore: because he also intended to be included in the animal he slaughtered and it is not clear which was slaughtered first.

chunks.en: and his goes out to the place of burning,
chunks.st: Therefore, his must be taken out to the place designated for burning;

chunks.en: and he does not need to bring Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: and he is exempt from performing the sacrifice of the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.en: If he said to them and they said to him,
chunks.st: If he said to them that if he is delayed they should include him in their Paschal lamb, and they said to him that if he finds the original offering he should slaughter it on their behalf,

chunks.en: they all eat from the first one.
chunks.st: all of them eat from the first sacrifice that was slaughtered.

chunks.en: And if it is not known which
chunks.st: And if it is not known which of them

chunks.en: of them was shechted first,
chunks.st: was slaughtered first,

chunks.en: both of them go out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: both of them must be taken out to the place designated for burning, and the entire group is exempt from participating in the Paschal lamb on the second Pesaḥ.

chunks.he: לֹא אָמַר לָהֶן וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לוֹ,
chunks.en: If he did not say to them and they did not say to him,
chunks.st: If he did not say anything to them and they did not say anything to him, meaning that neither side granted the other authority to slaughter a Paschal lamb on its behalf,

chunks.en: they are not responsible for each other.
chunks.explain: Each one eats from his own korban.
chunks.st: they are not responsible for each other,
chunks.stMore: and the members of the group eat their Paschal lamb while the individual sent to find the lost animal eats from his own offering. The reason for this is that the individual is registered only for the original offering, while the other members of the group withdrew from that lost offering by sacrificing a different Paschal lamb.

mishnayos.summary: Two groups' korbanos Pesach got mixed up and nobody knows which is whose. This mishnah teaches how they swap members so that everyone ends up signed up on the right korban.

chunks.en: Two groups whose korbanos Pesach got mixed up:
chunks.st: Two groups whose Paschal lambs have become intermingled
chunks.stMore: and they do not know which one belongs to which group should act in the following manner:

chunks.en: these take one for themselves
chunks.st: These members of the first group draw one of the animals separated as a Paschal lamb for themselves,

chunks.en: and these take one for themselves.
chunks.st: and those members of the second group draw one for themselves.

chunks.he: אֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: One of these comes over to those,
chunks.st: One of these, a member of one group, comes to those, the members of the other group,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מֵאֵלּוּ בָא לוֹ אֵצֶל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: and one of those comes over to these.
chunks.st: and one of those members of the second group comes to these members of the first group.

chunks.en: And this is what they say:
chunks.st: And this is what each group says to the member of the other group who has come to join them:

chunks.en: "If this korban Pesach is ours,
chunks.st: If this Paschal lamb that is now in our possession is ours,

chunks.he: יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלָּנוּ,
chunks.en: your hands are pulled away from yours and you are signed up on ours.
chunks.st: you are withdrawn from the Paschal lamb that was yours, and you are registered for our Paschal lamb and you may eat from it.

chunks.en: And if this korban Pesach is yours,
chunks.st: And if this Paschal lamb is yours, meaning that it actually belongs to the other group, including this individual,

chunks.he: יָדֵינוּ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ וְנִמְנֵינוּ עַל שֶׁלָּךְ.
chunks.en: our hands are pulled away from ours and we are signed up on yours."
chunks.st: we are hereby withdrawn from ours and we are registered for your Paschal lamb, which you agree to share with us.
chunks.stMore: The other group makes the same statement.

chunks.he: וְכֵן חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: And so too five groups of five people each,
chunks.st: And similarly, if there were five groups of five people each

chunks.en: or of ten people each,
chunks.st: or of ten people each,

chunks.he: מוֹשְׁכִין לָהֶן אֶחָד מִכָּל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה,
chunks.en: they take one from each and every group,
chunks.st: they draw one person from each and every group,

chunks.en: and they say the same thing.
chunks.st: and they say this statement mentioned in the case of two groups.
chunks.stMore: The remaining member or members of each group will grant the representatives of the other groups that have come to join them a share in the Paschal lamb, and they will acquire a share in it for themselves in case the animal they have chosen belonged originally to one of the other groups.

mishnayos.summary: Two people's korbanos Pesach got mixed up. This mishnah teaches how each one adds a new person, so they can swap and both be signed up on the right korban.

chunks.en: Two people whose korbanos Pesach got mixed up:
chunks.st: In the case of two individuals whose Paschal lambs became intermingled
chunks.stMore: and each person was the only one registered for his offering, what should they do?

chunks.en: this one takes one for himself,
chunks.st: This person draws one of the Paschal lambs for himself

chunks.en: and that one takes one for himself.
chunks.st: and that person draws one for himself;

chunks.he: זֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: This one signs up one person from the market with him,
chunks.st: this person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb

chunks.he: וְזֶה מַמְנֶה עִמּוֹ אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: and that one signs up one person from the market with him.
chunks.st: and that person registers someone from the marketplace with him on his Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: This one comes to that one,
chunks.st: Once this has been done, this one comes to that person from the marketplace who has been added to the other person’s sacrifice,

chunks.en: and that one comes to this one,
chunks.st: and that one comes to this person from the marketplace who has been added to the first person’s sacrifice,

chunks.en: and this is what they say:
chunks.st: and this is what they say:

chunks.en: "If this korban Pesach is mine,
chunks.st: If this Paschal lamb is mine,

chunks.he: יָדֶיךָ מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלְּךָ וְנִמְנֵיתָ עַל שֶׁלִּי.
chunks.en: your hands are pulled away from yours and you are signed up on mine.
chunks.st: you are withdrawn from yours and you are registered for mine,

chunks.en: And if this korban Pesach is yours,
chunks.st: and if this is your Paschal lamb,

chunks.he: יָדַי מְשׁוּכוֹת מִשֶּׁלִּי וְנִמְנֵיתִי עַל שֶׁלָּךָ:
chunks.en: my hands are pulled away from mine and I am signed up on yours."
chunks.st: I am withdrawn from mine and I am hereby registered for yours,
chunks.stMore: as described previously. The reason it is necessary for each individual to add an additional person to his Paschal lamb, is to ensure that when each person withdraws from his original Paschal lamb and registers for the other, no Paschal lamb will be left ownerless for any amount of time.

mishnayos.summary: On Erev Pesach, we do not eat close to the evening, so we can eat matzah with an appetite. At the Seder, even the poorest person leans and gets four cups of wine.

chunks.en: On Erev Pesach, close to Mincha time,
chunks.st: On the eve of Passover, adjacent to minḥa time,

chunks.en: a person should not eat until it gets dark.
chunks.explain: So he will eat the matzah at night with an appetite.
chunks.st: a person may not eat until dark,
chunks.stMore: so that he will be able to eat matza that night with a hearty appetite.

chunks.en: And even the poorest person in Israel should
chunks.st: Even the poorest of Jews should

chunks.en: not eat until he leans.
chunks.explain: He leans to the left, like free and rich people.
chunks.st: not eat the meal on Passover night until he reclines on his left side,
chunks.stMore: as free and wealthy people recline when they eat.

chunks.en: And they should not give him less than four
chunks.st: And the distributors of charity should not give a poor person less than four

chunks.en: cups of wine,
chunks.st: cups of wine for the Festival meal of Passover night.

chunks.en: even if he gets his food from the charity plate.
chunks.st: And this halakha applies even if the poor person is one of the poorest members of society and receives his food from the charity plate.

words.note: Food given to the poorest people.

mishnayos.summary: At the Seder, Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue which bracha comes first over the first cup: the bracha on the day (Kiddush) or the bracha on the wine.

chunks.en: They poured for him the first cup.
chunks.st: The attendants poured the wine of the first cup for the leader of the seder.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he says the bracha on the day,
chunks.explain: Kiddush for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: One recites the blessing over the sanctification of the day, i.e., the kiddush for the Festival: Who blesses Israel and the Festivals,

chunks.en: and after that he says the bracha on the wine.
chunks.st: and thereafter he recites the blessing over the wine: Who creates fruit of the vine.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he says the bracha on the wine,
chunks.st: One recites the blessing over the wine

chunks.en: and after that he says the bracha on the day.
chunks.st: and thereafter recites the blessing over the day.

mishnayos.stIntro: The tanna describes the beginning of the Passover seder.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah describes the foods brought to the Seder table: vegetables, matzah, maror, charoses, two cooked foods, and in the time of the Beis Hamikdash, the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: They brought food in front of him.
chunks.st: The attendants brought vegetables before the leader of the seder prior to the meal,
chunks.stMore: if there were no other vegetables on the table.

chunks.en: He dips the lettuce
chunks.st: He dips the ḥazeret into water or vinegar, to taste some food

words.note: Chazeres, used for maror.

chunks.en: before he gets to the maror that goes with the bread.
chunks.explain: Maror, which is eaten after the matzah.
chunks.st: before he reaches the dessert of the bread, i.e., the bitter herbs, which were eaten after the matza.

chunks.en: They brought in front of him matzah, lettuce,
chunks.st: They brought before him matza and ḥazeret

chunks.en: charoses, and two cooked foods,
chunks.st: and ḥaroset, and at least two cooked dishes in honor of the Festival.

words.note: A sweet dip for the maror.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין חֲרֹסֶת מִצְוָה.
chunks.en: even though charoses is not a mitzvah.
chunks.st: The tanna comments that this was the practice, although eating ḥaroset is not a mitzva but merely a custom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Tzadok says:

chunks.en: it is a mitzvah. And in the Beis Hamikdash they would bring in front of him
chunks.st: Actually, it is a mitzva to eat ḥaroset. And in the period when the Temple stood and they offered the Paschal lamb, they brought before him

chunks.en: the korban Pesach itself.
chunks.st: the body of the Paschal lamb.

mishnayos.summary: When the second cup is poured, the son asks Mah Nishtanah, and the father teaches him the story of leaving Mitzrayim.

chunks.en: They poured for him the second cup,
chunks.st: The attendants poured the second cup for the leader of the seder,

chunks.en: and here the son asks his father.
chunks.st: and here the son asks his father the questions about the differences between Passover night and a regular night.

chunks.en: And if the son does not understand enough,
chunks.st: And if the son does not have the intelligence to ask questions on his own,

chunks.en: his father teaches him:
chunks.st: his father teaches him the questions.
chunks.stMore: The mishna lists the questions:

chunks.he: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מִכָּל הַלֵּילוֹת,
chunks.en: Why is this night different from all other nights?
chunks.st: Why is this night different from all other nights?

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין חָמֵץ וּמַצָּה,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat chametz and matzah,
chunks.st: As on all other nights we eat leavened bread and matza as preferred;

chunks.en: this night only matzah.
chunks.st: on this night all our bread is matza.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין שְׁאָר יְרָקוֹת,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat all kinds of vegetables,
chunks.st: As on all other nights we eat other vegetables;

chunks.en: this night maror.
chunks.st: on this night we eat bitter herbs.
chunks.stMore: The mishna continues its list of the questions.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ אוֹכְלִין בָּשָׂר צָלִי,
chunks.en: On all other nights we eat meat roasted,
chunks.st: When the Temple was standing one would ask: As on all other nights we eat either roasted,

chunks.en: boiled, or cooked,
chunks.st: stewed, or cooked meat,

chunks.en: this night only roasted.
chunks.explain: The korban Pesach, in the time of the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: but on this night all the meat is the roasted meat of the Paschal lamb.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ מַטְבִּילִין פַּעַם אַחַת,
chunks.en: On all other nights we dip one time,
chunks.st: The final question was asked even after the destruction of the Temple: As on all other nights we dip the vegetables in a liquid during the meal only once;

chunks.en: this night two times.
chunks.st: however, on this night we dip twice.

chunks.en: And according to how much the son understands,
chunks.st: And according to the intelligence and the ability of the son,

chunks.en: his father teaches him.
chunks.st: his father teaches him about the Exodus.
chunks.stMore: When teaching his son about the Exodus.

chunks.en: He begins with the shame and ends with the praise,
chunks.explain: How bad it was for us, and how Hashem saved us.
chunks.st: He begins with the Jewish people’s disgrace and concludes with their glory.

chunks.en: and he explains from "An Arami tried to destroy my father,"
chunks.st: And he expounds from the passage: “An Aramean tried to destroy my father” (Deuteronomy 26:5), the declaration one recites when presenting his first fruits at the Temple,

chunks.en: until he finishes the whole parshah.
chunks.st: until he concludes explaining the entire section.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches that at the Seder we must explain Pesach, matzah and maror. Every person must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim, so we thank and praise Hashem.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel used to say,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel would say:

chunks.en: anyone who did not say three
chunks.st: Anyone who did not say

chunks.en: of these things on Pesach
chunks.st: these three matters on Passover

chunks.en: did not do his mitzvah.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation:

chunks.en: And they are:
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: Pesach, matzah,
chunks.st: matza,

chunks.en: and maror. Pesach,
chunks.st: and bitter herbs. When one mentions these matters, he must elaborate and explain them: The Paschal lamb is brought

chunks.en: because Hashem passed over
chunks.st: because the Omnipresent passed over [pasaḥ]

words.note: Literally "the Place."

chunks.en: the houses of our fathers in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: the houses of our forefathers in Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “That you shall say: It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s Paschal offering for He passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses” (Exodus 12:27).

chunks.he: מַצָּה, עַל שׁוּם שֶׁנִּגְאֲלוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם.
chunks.en: Matzah, because our fathers were redeemed in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel continues to explain: The reason for matza is because our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “And they baked the dough that they took out of Egypt as cakes of matzot, for it was not leavened, as they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual” (Exodus 12:39).

chunks.en: Maror, because the Mitzrim made bitter
chunks.st: The reason for bitter herbs is because the Egyptians embittered

chunks.en: the lives of our fathers in Mitzrayim.
chunks.st: our forefathers’ lives in Egypt,
chunks.stMore: as it is stated: “And they embittered their lives with hard service, in mortar and in brick; in all manner of service in the field, all the service that they made them serve was with rigor” (Exodus 1:14).

chunks.he: בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר חַיָּב אָדָם לִרְאוֹת
chunks.en: In every generation, a person must see
chunks.st: The tanna of the mishna further states: In each and every generation a person must view

chunks.he: אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְאִלּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
chunks.en: himself as if he left Mitzrayim,
chunks.st: himself as though he personally left Egypt,

chunks.en: as it says (Shemos 13),
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: "And you shall tell your son on that day, saying,
chunks.st: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying:

chunks.en: 'Because of this, Hashem did
chunks.st: It is because of this which the Lord did

chunks.en: for me when I left Mitzrayim.'"
chunks.st: for me when I came forth out of Egypt” (Exodus 13:8).
chunks.stMore: In every generation, each person must say: “This which the Lord did for me,” and not: This which the Lord did for my forefathers.

chunks.en: So we must thank,
chunks.st: The mishna continues with the text of the Haggadah. Therefore we are obligated to thank,

chunks.en: praise, glorify,
chunks.st: praise, glorify,

chunks.en: honor, raise up,
chunks.st: extol, exalt,

chunks.en: give glory, bless,
chunks.st: honor, bless,

chunks.en: lift up, and praise
chunks.st: revere, and laud [lekales]

chunks.en: the One who did for our fathers and for us
chunks.st: the One who performed for our forefathers and for us

chunks.en: all these miracles.
chunks.st: all these miracles:

chunks.en: He took us out from slavery to freedom,
chunks.st: He took us out from slavery to freedom,

chunks.en: from sadness to joy,
chunks.st: from sorrow to joy,

chunks.en: and from mourning to Yom Tov,
chunks.st: from mourning to a Festival,

words.note: Yom Tov.

chunks.en: and from darkness to great light,
chunks.st: from darkness to a great light,

chunks.en: and from being slaves to being redeemed.
chunks.st: and from enslavement to redemption.

chunks.en: And let us say before Him, Halleluyah!
chunks.st: And we will say before Him: Halleluya.
chunks.stMore: At this point one recites the hallel that is said on all joyous days. Since one does not complete hallel at this point in the seder, the mishna asks:

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue how much of Hallel is said before the meal. Then Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva teach how the bracha of redemption ends.

chunks.en: How far does he say?
chunks.explain: How much of Hallel before the meal.
chunks.st: Until where does one recite hallel?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: until "a happy mother of children."
chunks.st: Until “Who makes the barren woman dwell in her house as a joyful mother of children, halleluya” (Psalms 113:9).

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: until "the flint into a spring of water."
chunks.st: Until “Who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a fountain of waters” (Psalms 114:8).

words.note: A very hard rock.

chunks.en: And he ends with a bracha of redemption.
chunks.st: And one concludes this section of hallel with a blessing that refers to redemption.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says that although one should recite:

chunks.he: אֲשֶׁר גְּאָלָנוּ וְגָאַל אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם,
chunks.en: "Who redeemed us and redeemed our fathers from Mitzrayim,"
chunks.st: Who redeemed us and redeemed our forefathers from Egypt,

chunks.en: and he did not end with "Baruch Atah."
chunks.st: one who did so would not conclude with the formula: Blessed are You, Lord.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says that one recites a different version of this blessing:

chunks.he: כֵּן ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ יַגִּיעֵנוּ
chunks.en: "So may Hashem our God and the God of our fathers bring us
chunks.st: So too, the Lord our God and the God of our forefathers will bring us

chunks.he: לְמוֹעֲדִים וְלִרְגָלִים אֲחֵרִים הַבָּאִים לִקְרָאתֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: to other holidays and Yamim Tovim that come toward us in peace,
chunks.st: to future holidays and Festivals in peace,

chunks.en: happy in the building of Your city and joyful in Your service.
chunks.st: happy over the building of Your city and joyous in Your service.

chunks.en: And we will eat there from the korbanos
chunks.st: And there we will eat from the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: and from the korbanos Pesach," and so on,
chunks.st: and other offerings, etc.,

chunks.he: עַד בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה' גָּאַל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
chunks.en: until "Baruch Atah Hashem, who redeemed Israel."
chunks.st: until: Blessed are You, Lord, Who redeemed Israel.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what we say over the third and fourth cups, and when we may drink more wine.

chunks.en: They poured for him the third cup,
chunks.st: They poured for the leader of the seder the third cup of wine,

chunks.en: he says the bracha on his food.
chunks.explain: Birkas Hamazon.
chunks.st: and he recites the blessing over his food, Grace After Meals.

chunks.en: The fourth: he finishes Hallel over it,
chunks.st: Next, they pour him the fourth cup. He completes hallel over it, as he already recited the first part of hallel before the meal.

chunks.en: and he says over it the bracha of song.
chunks.st: And he also recites the blessing of the song at the end of hallel over the fourth cup.

chunks.en: Between these cups,
chunks.st: During the period between these cups, i.e., the first three cups established by the Sages,

chunks.en: if he wants to drink,
chunks.st: if one wishes to drink more

chunks.en: he may drink. Between the third and the fourth,
chunks.st: he may drink; however, between the third cup and the fourth cup one should

chunks.en: he should not drink.
chunks.st: not drink.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches not to eat anything after the korban Pesach, and what happens if people fell asleep during the meal.

chunks.en: And we do not end after the korban Pesach with afikoman.
chunks.explain: We do not eat dessert or snacks after it.
chunks.st: One does not conclude after the Paschal lamb with an afikoman.

chunks.en: If some of them fell asleep,
chunks.st: If some of the participants at the seder fell asleep, thereby interrupting their meal,

chunks.en: they may eat. All of them,
chunks.st: they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake. If the entire company fell asleep,

chunks.en: they may not eat.
chunks.st: they may not eat any more.
chunks.stMore: If they all fall asleep, this is considered a complete interruption, and if they were to resume their meal it would be akin to eating the offering in two different places.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: if they dozed, they may eat.
chunks.st: If they dozed they may eat from the Paschal lamb when they awake,

chunks.en: If they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.
chunks.st: but if they fell fast asleep they may not eat from it.

mishnayos.summary: The korban Pesach after midnight makes hands tamei. This mishnah also teaches whether the bracha on the korban Pesach counts for the chagigah, and the other way around.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach after midnight
chunks.st: The Paschal lamb after midnight

chunks.en: makes the hands tamei.
chunks.explain: After midnight it may not be eaten anymore.
chunks.st: renders one’s hands ritually impure,
chunks.stMore: as it becomes notar, an offering that remained after the time when they may be eaten has expired;

chunks.en: Piggul and nosar
chunks.st: and the Sages ruled that both piggul, offerings that were invalidated due to inappropriate intent while being sacrificed,

words.note: A korban made unfit by a wrong plan.
A korban left over after its time.

chunks.en: make the hands tamei.
chunks.st: and notar render one’s hands ritually impure.

chunks.en: If he said the bracha on the korban Pesach, it covers
chunks.st: If one recited the blessing over the Paschal lamb, which is: Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to eat the Paschal lamb, he has also exempted

chunks.en: the one on the korban.
chunks.st: himself from reciting a blessing over the Festival offering.
chunks.stMore: The blessing for the Festival peace-offering of the fourteenth of Nisan is: Who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to eat the offering.

words.note: The chagigah korban.

chunks.en: If he said the one on the korban,
chunks.st: However, if he recited the blessing over the Festival offering,

chunks.en: it does not cover the one on the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: he has not exempted himself from reciting a blessing over the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: this one does not cover that one,
chunks.st: This blessing does not exempt one from reciting a blessing over this one,

chunks.en: and that one does not cover this one.
chunks.st: and that blessing does not exempt that one, as there is a separate blessing for each offering.
